title: MHC reschedules Deepavali Day matches after public backlash
body: This is generated by AI, we welcome feedback.  The public and clubs expressed annoyance over Malaysian Hockey League (MHL) matches scheduled for Deepavali Day, 8 November. Two matches, Terengganu Hockey Team vs Armed Forces and TNB Thunderbolts vs Maybank, were originally set for 8 November. The Malaysian Hockey Confederation confirmed these matches would be rescheduled to 9 November and 14 November, respectively.

title: PublicInvest Research Headlines - 24 Sep 2026
body: Global: Inflation will linger and Fed will hike rates again, OECD says. Inflation around the world will be faster than forecast in 2027, an outlook that necessitates more tightening from the US to Australia. The Paris-based club of rich countries raised projections compared with June for consumer-price growth in every Group-of-20 economy apart from China and Saudi Arabia. Monetary policy across the globe may have to respond. The analysis underscores how the economic impact of the Middle East war unleashed by US President Donald Trump is now set to endure into the second half of his term in office. The OECD's assessment follows a round of tightening this month, with the US Fed, the ECB and BOJ all raising interest rates within little more than a week of each other. The organisation's officials reckon more such action is in the offing, while suggesting it won't match the aggressive policy moves seen in the wake of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine. (Bloomberg) US: Business activity at more than five-year high; inflation pressures building. US business activity raced to a more than five-year high in Sep, fueled by a surge in new orders, though strong demand strained supply chains and pushed prices higher. S&P Global's flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, increased to 58.4 this month. That was the highest level since July 2021 and followed a reading of 56.0 in August. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector. The rise in the PMI reflected strong gains in both the services and manufacturing sectors. The PMI was consistent with the economy growing at around a 5% annualised rate. It also noted a sharp rise in work backlogs and supply chain delays, pointing to a lack of operating capacity which fed through to higher prices. (Reuters) EU: Eurozone business activity hits three-year high on services. Private-sector activity in the euro area grew at the fastest pace in more than three years as the service sector unexpectedly improved. The Composite PMI compiled by S&P Global increased to 53.1 from 52 in August, well above the 50 threshold separating growth from contraction. Analysts in a Bloomberg survey had anticipated a small decline to 51.7. The region's two largest economies both exceeded expectations, with activity in Germany growing at the fastest pace since Oct 2025 and France unexpectedly expanding at the quickest in more than two years. The euro-area economy is showing greater resilience than expected to the Middle East conflict and the resulting jump in energy costs. How long it can resist such headwinds remains uncertain, however, with inflation at its highest level in almost three years and borrowing costs rising. (Bloomberg) UK: Business activity cools as inflation pressure ramps up ahead of budget. Growth in British business activity cooled this month and inflation pressure built, an awkward backdrop for Finance Minister John Healey ahead of his first budget next month. The S&P Global UK services PMI fell in Sep to 51.7 from 52.5 in August, a three-month low. A Reuters poll of economists had pointed to a reading of 52.0. Prices charged by services companies, the backbone of Britain's economy, rose at the fastest pace in four months. They also reported accelerating cost pressures following a rise in energy prices stemming from the escalating war in Iran. S&P Global's survey pointed to quarterly economic growth of around 0.1%, compared with 0.4% in 2Q.. (Reuters) Indonesia: Holds rate, boosting hedging incentives for rupiah. Indonesia's central bank kept its interest rate unchanged for a third straight meeting, choosing to rely on continued intervention and increased hedging incentives to support the rupiah in the face of higher oil prices and US yields. The new governor Destry Damayanti and her board held the BI-Rate at 5.75% on Wednesday as expected by 33 of 36 economists surveyed by Bloomberg. The rest had pencilled in a quarter-point hike. Bank Indonesia also further cut the premiums for conventional hedging swaps on portfolio investments by up to 25% and for domestic non-deliverable forwards by up to 30%. These perks are applicable for portfolio investments, foreign loans and foreign direct investments. The Indonesian rupiah and bonds held earlier gains after the decision, with the currency strengthening 0.4% to 17,800 per dollar to outperform regional peers on Wednesday. Stocks rallied further to 1.5%, the biggest rise in almost a month. (Bloomebrg) Singapore: Core inflation climbs to 2.2% in August. Singapore's core inflation rose in August, driven by higher inflation for services, retail and other goods, and food. Core inflation, which excludes private transport and accommodation to better reflect household expenses, came in at 2.2%, up from 2% in July. The figure was in line with a median estimate in a Bloomberg poll. Overall inflation increased to 2.3% in August, from 2.2% in July, as higher core inflation more than offset lower private transport inflation. Private transport inflation slowed to 7.5% in August, from 8% in July, due to a smaller increase in car prices. Meanwhile, accommodation inflation was unchanged at 0.8%, with housing rents increasing in August at the same pace as in July. Services inflation edged up to 2% in August, from 1.7% in July, as airfares and prices of point-to-point transport services climbed at a faster pace. (The Straits Times) CTOS: Detects cyber breach, limited consumer data accessed. CTOS Digital said that its cybersecurity system recently detected unauthorised access to an environment supporting its consumer business. Certain data files containing a limited subset of processed consumer information were accessed from the affected environment, the credit reporting agency said. However, CTOS did not disclose what specific personal information was accessed. (The Edge) Aneka Jaringan: Secures RM26m foundation works contract for 53-storey KL serviced apartment. Aneka Jaringan Holdings has won a RM26.2m contract for the foundation works for a 53-storey serviced apartment project at Jalan Yap Kwan Seng here. Aneka Jaringan said its wholly-owned subsidiary accepted the LoA for the project from WDA Architecture SB, acting on behalf of Exsim YKS 54 SB, a member company of Exsim Group. The contract for earthworks, piling, pile caps, retaining wall and sub-structure works commenced on Sept 15, is scheduled to conclude on Aug 14, 2028. (The Edge) Carimin Petroleum: Unit to acquire property in Sarawak worth RM21.1m. Carimin Petroleum's 90%-owned subsidiary, Sri Borneo Energy SB, proposes to acquire leasehold land and buildings in Sarawak from Sarwaja Timur SB for RM21.1m. Carimin Petroleum said its unit entered into a SPA with Sarwaja on Sept 14. The company said the acquisition would include the reactivation of the galvanising and metal fabrication business, leveraging the former plant's track record and customer recognition. (The Edge) Paragon Globe: Eyes RM1.69bn industrial park in Sedenak. Paragon Globe is pursuing a land acquisition in Sedenak, Johor, for a proposed industrial park with a preliminary GDV of RM1.69bn. The proposed development, located within the Kulai-Sedenak flagship zone of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), is expected to comprise industrial factories, commercial components and worker accommodation. (The Star) AYS Ventures: To sell 74% stake in Steelaris for SGD5.2m. AYS Ventures's indirect wholly-owned subsidiary Ann Yak Siong (Singapore) Pte Ltd (AYSS) has agreed to dispose of its 74% stake in Singapore-based Steelaris Pte Ltd to CosmoSteel Holdings Pte Ltd for SGD5.2m. AYS Ventures said AYSS will receive SGD1.8m in cash and 13.5m new CosmoSteel shares at an issue price of SGD0.25 each. (The Star) YTL Power: YTL AI Labs partners with NVIDIA to create dataset for training Malaysia-context AI. YTL AI Labs SB, a subsidiary of YTL Power International, announced the creation of a dataset of 1.35m synthetic personas that will help in the development of AI models that suit Malaysia's diversity. The dataset, called Nemotron-Personas-Malaysia, was developed in collaboration with tech giant Nvidia. (The Edge) Destini: Signs two-year pact with Siemens Mobility for digital railway MRO. Destini will collaborate with transit and rail technology company Siemens Mobility SB to realise its ambition of becoming a digitally enabled railway maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) service provider. The group's 70%-owned unit M Rail Technics SB (Railtec) has signed a two-year agreement with Siemens Mobility to establish a reliability control centre for data-driven MRO. (The Edge) The KLCI might open lower higher today as pressure from the US bond market hit a new level on Wall Street Wednesday after a surprisingly strong report on the economy raised worries about inflation, while oil prices halted their slide. The squeeze caused US stocks to sink. The S&P 500 fell 0.8% after finishing the prior day just 0.4% below its record set last month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 352 points, or 0.7%, while the Nasdaq composite sank 1.1% from its own all-time high. Stocks wilted after the yield on the 10-year Treasury jumped to 5.10% from 4.96% late Tuesday, which is a considerable move for the bond market. High yields undercut prices for stocks and other investments, while also slowing the economy by making it more expensive for everyone to borrow money. Wednesday's jump briefly sent the 10-year yield near 5.14%, back to where it was in 2007 before the global financial crisis caused yields to crater. Yields have been climbing since bottoming out in the COVID pandemic, and they've accelerated recently because of worries about high inflation, the US government's heavy debt and other concerns. Worries about inflation got a jolt Wednesday morning after a preliminary report suggested growth in US business activity surged to its strongest level in more than five years. That's an encouraging signal, to be sure, but it indicates the economy may have plenty of fuel for more inflation. In stock markets elsewhere, indices slipped across much of Europe and Asia. Stock indices fell 1% in Hong Kong and 0.4% in Shanghai ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to Washington, which is kicking off Wednesday. Back home, the KLCI lost 7.07 points or -0.4% to end at 1,676.43. title: ‘Ibu Janji Ambil Kami Di Sekolah, Tapi Dia Pergi Buat Selamanya’ | Medialahmy
body: GUA MUSANG – Hancur hati dua beradik apabila ibu yang dinanti untuk menjemput mereka pulang dari sekolah tidak kunjung tiba, sebaliknya mereka menerima berita duka apabila insan tersayang itu meninggal dunia akibat kemalangan. Nur Arissa Najla Mohd Shazuam, 13, dan Nur Amani Nuwairah Mohd Shazuam, 15, menanti penuh sabar selepas ibunya, Nor Hasyikim Daud, 34, berjanji mengambil mereka pulang dari Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Bandar Chiku. Nur Arissa Najla berkata, dia menerima berita kemalangan itu daripada seorang rakan ketika menunggu pada 1.40 tengah hari. “Ibu ada maklumkan akan ke Gua Musang dengan rakannya dan berjanji mengambil saya serta kakak dari sekolah. “Pada hari kejadian, saya menduduki tiga kertas peperiksaan dan sangat teruja untuk memberitahu ibu yang saya boleh jawab semua soalan subjek Sejarah. “Lebih setengah jam menanti ibu, namun tidak kunjung tiba, sebaliknya saya terima berita ibu kemalangan. “Saya nampak bapa saudara datang menjemput kami,” katanya ketika ditemui di Felda Chiku 5 di sini. Dalam kejadian Ahad lalu, Nor Hasyikim maut di lokasi kejadian apabila kenderaan dipandunya bertembung dengan lori 10 tan di Kilometer 40 Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Krai. Mangsa meninggal dunia akibat tersepit, manakala rakannya di tempat duduk penumpang hadapan cedera parah. Allahyarham turut meninggalkan seorang bayi Nur Aireen Nisrina berusia 11 bulan. Sementara itu, kakak kepada Nor Hasyikim, Siti Noraeshah Daud, 39, berkata, tiga beradik itu akan dijaga ibunya dengan bantuan adik-beradik lain. “Sejak setahun lalu arwah membesarkan tiga anaknya dengan bekerja di kantin asrama SMK Bandar Chiku. “Selepas ini kami akan bersama-sama menjaga dan membesarkan tiga anak perempuan arwah,” katanya. Orang ramai yang ingin memberi sumbangan boleh menyalurkan ke akaun Bank CIMB milik Siti Noraeshah Daud bernombor 7601845122. Sumber – Berita Harian

title: FBM KLCI expansion to improve sector diversification: CIMB Securities
body: KUALA LUMPUR: The proposed expansion of the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) to 50 constituents is expected to materially improve sector diversification. CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said the expanded benchmark will have lower exposure to financial services and utilities, while increasing representation across industrials, technology, consumer discretionary, energy, real estate and consumer staples. This is consistent with CIMB Securities' previous simulation, which estimated that the 20 new constituents could account for around 15.6 per cent of the expanded index at full inclusion. "We remain positive on the structural change as it should create a more representative Malaysian benchmark and broaden institutional exposure beyond the existing large-cap sectors," it said in a note. Meanwhile, CIMB Securities said FTSE clarified that full market capitalisation determines final stock selection, while free float determines index weights. Since passive FBM KLCI-tracking assets under management are relatively small and inclusion is phased at 50 per cent in December 2026 and 100 per cent in June 2027, the firm expects the near-term flow impact to be more stock-specific than market-wide. "The FBM70 will be reduced to 50 constituents and renamed FBM Mid-cap Index on Dec 21 while the FBM100 remains unchanged. "Derivatives specifications remain unchanged, while FTSE Russell is reviewing a relaxation of the fast-entry threshold for large initial public offerings," it said. CIMB Securities expects details to be reflected in an updated FTSE Bursa Malaysia Index Series Ground Rules notice once finalised at the end of this month. "Key dates to watch are the Nov 23, 2026 ranking cut-off, Dec 3, 2026 constituent announcement and Dec 21, 2026 first-stage inclusion, with full inclusion on June 21, 2027," it added.

title: Bursa Malaysia pulih pada dagangan awal hari ini
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia meningkat semula untuk dibuka tinggi pada Jumaat didorong oleh hasil Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang rendah dan sentimen Rizab Persekutuan (Fed) yang berhati-hati memberikan kelegaan kepada pelabur. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 1.49 mata atau 0.09 peratus kepada 1,631.85 daripada 1,630.36 semasa ditutup pada Khamis. Indeks dibuka tinggi 3.51 mata kepada 1,633.87. Dalam pasaran secara menyeluruh, kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 239 berbanding 137 manakala 270 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,127 tidak diniagakan dan 24 yang lain digantung. Jumlah dagangan sebanyak 173.94 juta saham bernilai RM95.98 juta. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng, berkata penurunan terkini telah mendorong indeks kembali kepada keadaan terlebih jual, yang boleh menggalakkan aktiviti belian saham pada harga rendah. "Bagaimanapun, dengan situasi jualan asing yang dilaporkan, kami percaya sebarang peningkatan awal mungkin kekal sederhana. "Namun demikian, aliran penurunan membuka peluang untuk membeli secara terpilih saham yang mempunyai asas kukuh terutamanya dalam kalangan bank yang mapan, syarikat utiliti dan syarikat semikonduktor," katanya kepada Bernama. Pak Leng berkata, pemulihan yang lebih mampan memerlukan penyertaan yang lebih baik daripada kaunter saham wajaran tinggi dan peningkatan jumlah saham daripada pelbagai sektor. Oleh itu, beliau menjangka dagangan berhati-hati hari ini dalam julat 1,625 hingga 1,640. Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Maybank mendatar pada RM9.95, Public Bank dan CIMB, masing-masing menurun satu sen kepada RM4.66 dan RM7.68, Tenaga Nasional naik empat sen kepada RM12.94 dan IHH Healthcare meningkat satu sen kepada RM7.71. Dalam dagangan aktif, Zetrix AI, Jaks Resources dan Genetec, masing-masing kekal tidak berubah pada 16.5 sen, 18 sen dan 32.5 sen, V.S Industry naik satu sen kepada 28 sen, bagaimanapun Kinergy Advancement menurun setengah sen kepada 39.5 sen. Kaunter paling untung ialah Malaysian Pacific Industries meningkat 58 sen kepada RM41.70, Hengyuan Refining naik 19 sen kepada RM3.83, Petronas Chemicals menokok 15 sen kepada RM4.28 serta UWC dan MI Technovation, masing-masing menambah 10 sen kepada RM7.20 dan RM5.36. Kaunter paling rugi termasuklah MISC menurun 14 sen kepada RM7.54, LPI Capital, Hong Leong Industries, MNRB dan RHB Bank, masing-masing merosot empat sen kepada RM12.80, RM16.10, RM2.78 dan RM7.43. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 meningkat 75.93 mata kepada 17,434.91, Indeks FBM Emas naik 17.18 mata kepada 12,160.71 dan Indeks FBM Top 100 menokok 21.58 mata kepada 11,954.73. Indeks FBM Emas Shariah menambah 34.76 mata kepada 12,047.77 dan Indeks FBM ACE naik 18.61 mata kepada 5,501.58. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk Perindustrian dan Perkhidmatan meningkat 1.10 mata kepada 178.83, Indeks Tenaga naik 9.45 mata kepada 844.46, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan menurun 26.33 mata kepada 19,034.58 manakala Indeks Perladangan menokok 2.75 mata kepada 9,029.32. -BERNAMA

title: 债券收益率上升打击银行股 马银行9个月来首次跌破10令吉
body: 债券收益率上升打击银行股 马银行9个月来首次跌破10令吉 （吉隆坡1日讯）债券收益率上升，拖累银行股普遍下跌，而马银行（Malayan Banking Bhd）（KL:MAYBANK）股价更是近9个月来首次跌破10令吉。 收益率上升通常对银行不利，因为银行持有的债券价格下跌，导致更大的账面亏损，这会侵蚀资本，并迫使银行在出售时确认损失。银行还需要提高利率以吸引存款人，从而导致融资成本上升。 艾芬黄氏投资银行今日在报告中指出，这将影响银行的短期非利息收入以及资本比率。 马来西亚资产规模最大的银行马银行连续第三天下跌，收盘下跌0.4%，报9.95令吉。联昌国际集团（CIMB Group Holdings Bhd）（KL:CIMB）和丰隆银行（Hong Leong Bank Bhd）（KL:HLBANK）各跌逾1%。 大马交易所金融服务指数下跌至10个月以来的最低水平。 本月初，美联储3年来首次加息，导致马来西亚10年期基准国债收益率一度高达4.18%，之后有所回落。 越来越多经济学家预计，国家银行将在11月举行的年度最后一次货币政策评估会议上调高隔夜政策利率（OPR）。 艾芬黄氏指出，收益率上升通常会导致企业债券收益率上升，这也会与银行及其他企业的融资决策挂钩，进而影响银行的手续费收入。 根据该研究机构的分析，马银行和安联银行（Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd）（KL:ABMB）拥有最长的债券期限——即债券以现金流形式偿还本金所需的时间，同时也衡量了其对利率变动的敏感性。 与此同时，大众银行（Public Bank Bhd）（KL:PBBANK）和丰隆银行的期限最短。就资本充足率而言，马银行、兴业银行（RHB Bank Bhd）（KL:RHBBANK）和联昌国际集团的降幅可能最大，而大众银行和丰隆银行的降幅最小，因为它们的投资组合期限较短。 （编译：魏素雯） The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: Bursa Malaysia Opens Higher Tracking Wall Street Gains
body: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 – Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Monday morning, tracking overnight gains on Wall Street as softer US payroll growth eased investor concerns regarding an immediate interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. At 9:10 AM, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) climbed 5.01 points, or 0.31 per cent, to 1,635.88 compared to last Friday’s closing figure of 1,630.87. The benchmark index initially opened 2.55 points higher at 1,633.42. Across the broader market, advancing counters outpaced decliners 224 to 158, while 337 counters remained unchanged, 2,054 untraded, and 24 suspended. Total market turnover stood at 206.30 million shares valued at RM98.78 million. Key market indices and sector performances during early trade included: - Heavyweight Movement: Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB, and Tenaga Nasional each gained four sen to reach RM10.06, RM4.70, RM7.69, and RM13.00, respectively. Conversely, IHH Healthcare shed six sen to RM7.74. - Top Active Stocks: VS Industry advanced three sen to 32 sen, Notion VTec gained four sen to 74.5 sen, GB Bond edged up half-a-sen to 23.5 sen, SFP Tech added one sen to 28.5 sen, and Dagang NeXchange traded flat at 51.5 sen. - Top Gainers: Samaiden surged 19 sen to RM3.03, UWC gained 16 sen to RM7.73, Critical Holdings rose 15 sen to RM2.61, Mi Technovation moved up nine sen to RM5.30, and Solarvest advanced eight sen to RM4.25. - Top Decliners: Nestle led losses, dropping 32 sen to RM89.20, followed by Vitrox (down 14 sen to RM10.32), Kobay Technology (down 12 sen to RM2.18), Kelington (down five sen to RM8.58), and YTL Power International (down four sen to RM5.64). - Index & Sector Breakdown: The Financial Services Index gained 97.59 points to 19,138.10, the Energy Index added 2.57 points to 835.60, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.59 of a point to 179.11, and the Plantation Index moved up 2.23 points to 9,058.78. The FBM Mid 70 Index climbed 28.14 points to 17,510.07, the FBM Emas Index rose 33.81 points to 12,204.38, and the FBM ACE Index improved 31.41 points to 5,560.87. –NMT

title: Stock Today: Maybank Dips 0.2% Despite New Wealth Advisory Initiative
body: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) shares fell 0.19% to RM10.40 as of 12.35 pm, after the bank and Asian Banking School (ABS) signed an agreement to explore a professional certification framework for wealth advisory in Malaysia.  The stock opened at RM10.44 and moved between an intraday high of RM10.48 and a low of RM10.38. Some 4.77 million shares changed hands.  Maybank had closed at RM10.42 in the previous trading session, putting the latest price two sen lower.  The proposed ABS Wealth Advisory & Management Certification Programme is intended to establish an industry-recognised benchmark for wealth advisory professionals in banking.  If launched, the programme would be Malaysia’s first industry-wide professional certification framework dedicated to wealth advisory, with the first intake expected in the second half of 2027.  Maybank will serve as the founding industry partner while ABS will oversee the standards, assessment and certification process.  Maybank plans to incorporate the programme into its Maybank Wealth Academy, linking the certification with structured learning and workplace development.  The two parties will also explore extending relevant certification pathways to wealth professionals across the region

title: HLB Islamic Berjaya Lonjak Pendapatan Usahawan Berpendapatan Rendah Langkawi Sebanyak 94%
body: KUALA LUMPUR, 23 SEPTEMBER 2026 – Selaras dengan komitmen untuk memperkasakan ekosistem perantaraan berasaskan nilai (“Value-based Intermediation” atau “VBI”), HLB Islamic (atau “Bank”) telah menyalurkan pembiayaan sebanyak RM138,600 kepada perusahaan sosial SURI Inspirasi (“SURI”) di bawah kerangka iTEKAD Bank Negara Malaysia (“BNM”). Inisiatif ini secara langsung menyumbang kepada peningkatan purata pendapatan bulanan sebanyak 94% serta menjana jumlah pendapatan baharu melebihi RM14,000 bagi usahawan yang menyertai program “Sustainable Reliable Income” (“SRI”) anjuran SURI. HLB Islamic Tingkatkan Pendapatan Usahawan Sebanyak 94% Melalui Program SRI Program SRI memperkasakan komuniti berpendapatan rendah untuk mengitar semula sisa fabrik menjadi barangan fesyen yang unik, yang secara langsung mewujudkan peluang pekerjaan dan memupuk semangat keusahawanan di samping mempromosikan fesyen sifar sisa serta pemerkasaan komuniti. Usahawan yang terlibat, yang majoriti ibu tunggal berpendapatan rendah, telah menghasilkan 1,000 pasang pakaian seragam sekolah untuk pelajar bagi lima buah sekolah di Langkawi, sekali gus menjana penjimatan sebanyak RM30,000 bagi keluarga tempatan. HLB Islamic meraikan pencapaian ini menerusi penyerahan mesin jahit berkualiti tinggi kepada para usahawan yang terlibat, menandakan peralihan daripada pembelajaran di dalam bilik darjah kepada pemilikan perniagaan secara aktif. Menurut Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif HLB Islamic, “Visi kami mengenai pengurusan kewangan berteraskan Hayat @ HLB Islamic, di mana pengurusan harta dilihat sebagai satu perjalanan yang bermula dengan Penciptaan Harta. Melalui kerjasama dengan SURI, kami menyediakan alat dan latihan asas yang diperlukan oleh komuniti untuk mencungkil potensi keusahawanan mereka. Kami berharap usaha ini akan menjadi pemangkin kepada perjalanan pembinaan kekayaan berterusan ke arah kebebasan kewangan yang bakal memperkayakan komuniti untuk generasi akan datang.” Kejayaan ini menandakan satu pencapaian penting dalam kerjasama berterusan antara HLB Islamic dan SURI, yang mula menyertai ekosistem Bank ini sebagai peserta inisiatif HLB Jumpstart. Diperkenalkan bagi memupuk perusahaan sosial Malaysia yang berimpak tinggi menerusi bimbingan komersial, penjenamaan, serta pembinaan kapasiti digital, HLB Jumpstart telah menyediakan kerangka awal kepada SURI untuk memperluas operasinya. Hal ini membuktikan strategi jangka panjang Bank dalam memupuk usaha sosial menjadi rakan pelaksana berdikari yang mampu memberikan impak yang lebih meluas. title: India’s Palm Oil Tax Cut Could Boost Earnings For Local Planters, CIMB
body: India’s decision to halve import duties on crude palm oil (CPO) could support demand for Malaysian palm oil and provide some relief to plantation companies, although stronger competition from sunflower oil may limit the upside, according to CIMB Securities.  In its latest plantation sector report, CIMB said India reduced the basic import duty on CPO to 5% from 10%, effective Sept 24, as the country seeks to ease domestic edible oil prices ahead of its September-to-November festive season.  India also cut the duty on crude soybean oil to 5% and eliminated the 10% duty on crude sunflower oil.  The changes are particularly relevant to Malaysia, with India accounting for approximately 17% of Malaysia’s palm oil export volume in 2025, making it an important market for the country’s plantation industry.  Higher CPO Prices Could Benefit Malaysian Planters  CIMB said lower import duties should reduce the landed cost of CPO in India, potentially encouraging higher palm oil consumption and imports.  However, the research house cautioned that the larger duty reduction for sunflower oil could improve its competitiveness against palm oil, limiting any significant shift in Indian demand towards CPO.  Before the announcement, CPO was already trading at a price advantage in the Indian market. As at Sept 18, its landed price stood at approximately US$1,265 per tonne, compared with US$1,314 for soybean oil and US$1,380 for sunflower oil.  CIMB expects the benefits for Malaysian plantation companies to come primarily through firmer CPO prices rather than a substantial increase in export volumes.  Upstream producers such as Johor Plantations Group, Genting Plantations, Hap Seng Plantations, Ta Ann Holdings and United Malacca have greater earnings sensitivity to higher CPO prices.  Integrated plantation groups, including SD Guthrie, IOI Corporation and Kuala Lumpur Kepong, could also benefit from stronger upstream margins.  Crude Palm Oil Retains Advantage Over Refined Products  CIMB noted that India has maintained a sizeable import duty differential between crude and refined palm oil, which continues to favour CPO imports for processing by Indian refiners.  The basic import duty on refined palm oil was reduced to 27.5% from 32.5%, compared with the new 5% duty on CPO.  As a result, CIMB expects the impact on Malaysian downstream refiners to remain broadly neutral.  The research house maintained its CPO price forecasts at RM4,450 per tonne for 2026 and RM4,550 for 2027, alongside its Overweight rating on the Malaysian plantation sector.

title: El Niño could worsen Malaysia’s power, water stress, says CIMB Securities
body: El Niño could worsen Malaysia’s power, water stress, says CIMB Securities KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 7): Hotter and drier conditions from El Niño could put greater pressure on Malaysia’s electricity and water systems into 2027, according to CIMB Securities. The research house said El Niño is expected to persist into early 2027 and peak between March and May, potentially lifting electricity demand for cooling while worsening water shortages. It said Malaysia is particularly exposed as electricity demand is already rising, while about 37% of treated water is lost through non-revenue water (NRW). “Hotter and drier conditions could further strain both systems, strengthening the need for cooling efficiency, water conservation, and better infrastructure management,” CIMB said. Malaysia’s peak electricity demand is projected to increase to 33.5 gigawatts (GW) by 2035 from 21.3GW in 2026, while data centres could account for 31% of Peninsular Malaysia’s electricity demand by then. CIMB said hotter weather could further increase cooling demand across commercial buildings, industrial facilities and data centres, adding to the country’s underlying electricity load growth. On the water side, Malaysia’s NRW rate remained high at 37.1% in 2024, meaning more than one-third of treated water was lost before reaching consumers. The losses are estimated to cost more than RM2 billion annually. Water stress is already visible in some areas, with two of the 49 dams monitored nationwide at critical levels as at Aug 31, namely the Muda Dam in Kedah and Sungai Pagar Dam in Labuan. CIMB said the government’s RM2.5 billion National NRW Programme and RM1.7 billion allocation under the 13th Malaysia Plan to replace about 1,800km of critical water pipes should support efforts to improve water efficiency. The research house named KJTS Group Bhd (KL:KJTS) and Insights Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB) as its preferred beneficiaries of the theme. KJTS offers direct exposure to rising cooling demand through its cooling energy and energy-efficiency businesses, while Insights Analytics provides digital water solutions including leak detection, pressure management and smart metering. CIMB maintained “buy” calls on both companies, with target prices of RM1.35 for KJTS and RM1.95 for Insights Analytics. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: EPF Disposes 10 Million Maybank Shares
body: The Employees Provident Fund (EPF) has disposed of 10 million shares in Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), reducing its direct shareholding in Malaysia’s largest banking group to 12.045%.  Maybank said the disposal took place on Sept 22 through Citigroup Nominees (Tempatan) Sdn Bhd, under an account held for the EPF.  Following the transaction, the retirement fund’s direct interest in Maybank stood at approximately 1.46 billion shares, representing 12.045% of the bank’s issued share capital.  The filing did not disclose the disposal price or total transaction value.  The EPF remains a substantial shareholder in Maybank following the disposal.  Maybank shares closed at 10.22, dropping close to 10% over the last six months.

title: Bursa Malaysia rebounds in early trade, investors remain cautious
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia rebounded in early trade on Friday, tracking Wall Street’s overnight recovery, although analysts expect investors to remain cautious and selective amid lingering concerns over US bond yields and oil prices.  Overnight, US stocks recovered from early losses to close slightly higher on Thursday as a global bond selloff eased, pulling Treasury yields back from multi-decade highs. Back home, the FBM KLCI rebounded in early trade, gaining 5.37 points, or 0.33%, to 1,635.73 at 9.27am, supported by gains in selected heavyweights including banking, healthcare, energy and industrial stocks. title: MACC Remands Corporate Brothers in RM10m Investment Probe, Seizes 15 Luxury Cars Among Others
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Two corporate figures, who are brothers, are being remanded for five days over an alleged abuse of position involving an investment of about RM10 million. The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) obtained the remand order, effective from Thursday until next Monday (Oct 5), from Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court on Thursday morning. According to a source, the two men, in their 40s and 50s and carrying the titles of Datuk Seri and Datuk Wira respectively, were detained at about 9pm on Wednesday after giving their statements at the MACC headquarters here. Initial investigations found that the duo were suspected of acting in collusion in the alleged offence in late 2020. “They are also believed to have colluded with an officer of an education-based foundation to approve an investment of about RM10 million in an investment company owned by the elder brother,” the source told Bernama. The MACC also seized 15 luxury cars, 12 high-powered motorcycles, five luxury watches, three bracelets and about RM30,000 in cash. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the matter when contacted and said the case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009. title: 前一日大跌后马股周五止跌微涨，外资撤退压力未除，银行股成重要观察区
body: 经历周四暴跌后，马股周五终于止住跌势，但反弹力度极弱。富时隆综指（FBM KLCI）最终收报1,630.87点，仅涨0.51点或0.03%，基本属于平盘。这意味着周四大跌20.81点后，指数并没有出现明显的技术性反攻。 一、宏观与资金面：真正压力仍是外资 今天市场最值得注意的并不是KLCI上涨0.03%，而是外资撤退背后的结构性压力仍未解除。 BIMB指出，马股大型股未来1至3个月仍可能面对卖压。周四外资净卖达到RM2.28亿，截至9月底，外国投资者持有马来西亚证券的比例已经降至17.8%。分析师认为，近期跌势并非单纯银行股调整，而是全球债息偏高、外资流出及整体风险偏好下降共同造成。 银行股尤其重要，因为银行约占KLCI市值40%至45%，因此马银行（MAYBANK）、联昌国际（CIMB）、大众银行（PBBANK）等大型银行只要出现1%至2%的调整，就足以明显影响指数。 👉 2026年10月2日马股盘后剖析 | PRO 专属内容… 🔒 升级 PRO 解锁完整内容 → 订阅 PRO ← 已是 PRO请 Login

title: Nearly 9,500 buildings across Malaysia must appoint fire safety managers from April 2027, Bomba D-G says
body: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises.   Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK).   “From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises,” he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank here today.

title: Smoky Singapore gears up to talk money ahead of F1
body: SINGAPORE, Oct 5 (Reuters) - Regional, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are meeting in Singapore for a slew of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Grand Prix as haze continues to shroud the city-state. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, famed investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, co-founder of the family-backed cryptocurrency business, are expected, while hundreds of thousands of Formula 1 fans will converge on the island. The night race through the city streets and some 40 sideline events are typically a global showcase for Singapore and hotel room rates have soared. The Fullerton Bay Hotel next to the race track is charging S$5,030 ($3,933) a night for a room that typically costs $1,460. This year the pall from Indonesia's most intense fires in more than a decade will probably form part of the backdrop. Air quality was forecast at the "high moderate to low unhealthy" range on Monday by Singapore's environment agency. No longer-range forecast was provided for Sunday's Grand Prix. Singapore's tourism board said F1 and its surrounding events had "strong momentum" reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. Jitters in financial markets where bond prices are slumping and sentiment around on AI is shifting from euphoric to cautious will occupy investors and business chiefs at the Forbes CEO Conference andMilken Asia Summit, which runs from Wednesday. Trump, a co-founder of crypto venture World Liberty Financial, is due to speak at the TOKEN2049 cryptocurrency event with digital asset markets fragile following a bruising 12 months. A hoped-for regulatory framework failed last month to clear the US Senate, in part as President Donald Trump's personal crypto dealings became a flashpoint for Democrats. Despite a recent bounce, the total value of the cryptocurrency market is down about a quarter over the last 12 months to $3 trillion, according to data aggregator CoinGecko. Still, organisers say their event is nearly sold out with 25,000 attendees expected, the same as last year. The Straits Times reported that about 90,000 "c-suite," or top ranking, executives will be in town. F1 generates around S$145 million in incremental tourism receipts for Singapore each year, according to official estimates. Maybank economistChua Hak Bin expects it to hit S$160 million this year, along with "wider economic benefits" from deals struck at sideline events. ($1 = 1.2794 Singapore dollars) (Reporting by Xinghui Kok and Tom Westbrook; Editing by Kim Coghill)

title: Maybank Group Sustainability Week 2026 advances net zero ambitions through capacity building and collective action | Maybank
body: In its third year, MGSW 2026 recognised over 1000 certified sustainability practitioners & continues to inspire greater net zero action across the Group Maybank recently organised the Maybank Group Sustainability Week (MGSW) 2026, a three-day sustainability-focused programme held from 21 to 23 September 2026 at Menara Merdeka Maybank. Under the theme “Net Zero. From Commitment to Action”, MGSW 2026 focuses on advancing Maybank’s net zero journey through capacity building, deepening sustainability awareness and strengthening capabilities, in line with the Group’s ROAR30 sustainability ambitions. MGSW 2026 saw Maybankers across the Group participate in two key events; ‘Net Zero Week’, which featured a series of learning, engagement and experiential activities, and the ‘Maybank Sustainability Practitioner Certification (MSPC) Open Day’ and ‘Grand Conferment Ceremony’, which celebrated over 1,000 certified sustainability practitioners and inspiring Maybankers to advance in their sustainability journey. The event saw the attendance of Dato' Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, President & Group CEO Maybank, Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Group Chief Sustainability Officer Maybank, Board of Directors and Group EXCO members of Maybank, Dato’ Ir. Ts. (Dr.) Izwan Hasli Mohd Ibrahim, CEO PNB Merdeka Ventures, Muazzam Mohamad, Head of Corporate Sustainability & Stewardship PNB, Leo Pui Yong, Chief Sustainability Officer Tenaga Nasional Berhad and Edey Suresh Kumar Manikam, Board Director at Large UN Global Compact Network Malaysia, Brunei & Cambodia (UNGCMBC). Dato' Sri Khairussaleh Ramli said “As we advance in our sustainability journey, MGSW 2026 reflects our continued focus on enabling our people to support our customers' transition journeys to net zero through stronger knowledge and mindsets. Ultimately, our commitment to capacity building will in turn help our customers transition responsibly and sustainably, strengthen our communities and drive meaningful sustainability impact.” A key highlight of MGSW 2026 was the MSPC Grand Conferment Ceremony, which honoured 36 MSPC Level 3 Red Belt graduates from across the Group for their achievements and continued commitment in sustainability. Developed in partnership with UNGCMBC, the MSPC programme was introduced in 2023 with the vision of building a future-ready sustainability workforce. Through its four-tier certification pathway comprising Level 1 White, Level 2 Green, Level 3 Red and Level 4 Black Belt levels, the programme combines sustainability knowledge with practical application to equip Maybankers with the capabilities needed to drive sustainability initiatives across the organisation. Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, President & Group CEO Maybank (Center in blue batik), Dato’ Ir. Ts. (Dr.) Izwan Hasli Mohd Ibrahim, CEO PNB Merdeka Ventures (In red tie) and Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Group Chief Sustainability Officer Maybank (In black blazer with glasses) posing with the MSPC Level 1 White Belt recipients at the MSPC Grand Conferment ceremony during the MGSW 2026. As the entry level of the MSPC programme, the certification equips Maybankers with the foundational knowledge and capabilities needed to drive sustainability initiatives across the Group. A key highlight of the MSPC ceremony was the recognition of the 36 MSPC Level 3 Red Belt graduates from across the Group. Since its inception, MSPC has grown into a network of sustainability practitioners across the Group, spanning more than 60 cohorts and expands beyond Malaysia to Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines and Cambodia. To date, the programme has enrolled more than 2,300 participants and certified 1,755 practitioners. Maybankers came together throughout the three-day MGSW 2026 to learn, engage and take action on sustainability through a diverse range of interactive workshops, experiential activities, sharing sessions and challenges, reflecting the Group’s commitment to advancing its net zero journey under the theme “Net Zero. From Commitment to Action.” As a pioneering initiative and a first of its kind in the industry, MSPC is a sustainability capability programme built on a structured belting system, demonstrating how a financial institution can systematically empower its people with the knowledge, skills and credibility needed to deliver sustainable impact. Maybankers participated in a weaving activity at the Women Eco Weavers booth by Maybank Foundation during the MGSW 2026, transforming used fabric into handcrafted products while promoting how traditional craftsmanship can support waste reduction and sustainable livelihood. “The MSPC ceremony marks another significant milestone in our journey towards becoming the sustainability leader in ASEAN as it is ultimately a celebration of our people. It recognises Maybankers who have committed themselves to developing the knowledge and skills needed to advance our sustainability ambitions. It also reflects how far we have progressed, from building awareness and advocacy to strengthening action and accountability across the Group.” said Dato' Sri Khairussaleh Ramli. MGSW 2026 also saw the launch of the ‘Plastic Bottle Recycling’ initiative between Maybank, PNB and PNB Merdeka Ventures to encourage greater environmental responsibility among occupants of Menara Merdeka Maybank. The initiative was launched by Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, Dato’ Izwan Hasli and Muazzam Mohamad through a symbolic recycling activity. As part of the initiative, dedicated plastic bottle recycling bins will be deployed across Menara Merdeka Maybank to encourage proper waste segregation and foster a greener, more environmentally conscious community. Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, President & Group CEO of Maybank, together with Muazzam Mohamad and Dato’ Ir. Ts. (Dr.) Izwan Hasli Mohd Ibrahim, officiates the launch of the Plastic Bottle Recycling initiative through a symbolic recycling activity during MGSW 2026. The programme featured a diverse range of learning, engagement, and experiential activities through initiatives such as Net Zero Zone, MSPC Experience Zone, Sustainability Marketplace, Upcycling Activities, Sustainability Tree, the Relationship Manager’s Net Zero Challenge, and #MaybankCares Points. Maybankers participated in the creation of reusable tote bags made from used clothing at the ‘Upcycling booth’ during the MGSW 2026, highlighting the importance of waste reduction, resource circularity and sustainable everyday practices. A series of expert-led discussions, workshops and sharing sessions covered topics such as “Talk to Traction: Solving the Net Zero Equation Across Sustainability, Business and Law.”, “From Energy Optimisation to Net Zero”, Menara Merdeka Maybank Green Building Sharing Session and Social Impact Partners’ Day. Concurrently, the Etiqa Sustainability Day was also held in conjunction with MGSW 2026, where they hosted workshops, sharing sessions and a Sustainability Bazaar at Dataran Maybank. Maybankers participated in expert-led discussions, workshops and knowledge-sharing sessions during Maybank Group Sustainability Week (MGSW) 2026, which covered topics ranging from net zero transition and energy optimisation to sustainable building practices and social impact, aimed at strengthening sustainability knowledge and action across the Group. Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin said “MGSW demonstrates the growing momentum of sustainability within Maybank. The enthusiasm and participation shown by Maybankers throughout the week reinforces our belief that continued progress is driven by a shared sense of purpose and responsibility. We are encouraged by this momentum and are confident it will continue to shape the way sustainability is embraced across the Group.” Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Group Chief Sustainability Officer Maybank (Center in Black blazer) sharing a light moment with participants of the Sustainable Manager Portfolio Challenge during the MGSW 2026. The interactive competition simulated real-world portfolio management scenarios, challenging participants to balance profitability, business growth and sustainability considerations in their decision-making. As part of its commitment in transitioning towards a low-carbon economy, Maybank has achieved a cumulative 58.9% reduction in operational carbon emissions since 2021, marking significant progress towards its target of a 61% reduction by 2026. The achievement reflects the Group’s continued efforts to reduce its environmental footprint while advancing its long-term ambitions of achieving carbon neutrality by 2030 and net zero emissions by 2050.

title: Tenaga Nasional Tells Analysts Extra Subsidy Is One-off, Mulls Permanent Solutions
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 23): Tenaga Nasional Bhd (KL:TENAGA) said the extra subsidy earmarked for households is a one-off measure, and the national electric utility is mulling tweaks to its charges to better shield consumers. The initial estimate of up to RM150 million in costs to subsidise consumers from rising electricity bills is conservative and the actual cost may be lower for the company, according to several analysts that attended an investor briefing by Tenaga Nasional on Tuesday. Tenaga Nasional stressed that “this is a one-off corporate contribution outside the regulatory framework, rather than a change to the revenue-cap or price-cap mechanism”, BIMB Securities said in a post-briefing note. The briefing follows a decline in Tenaga Nasional’s share price as investors priced in earnings impact after the company agreed to absorb the impact from the electricity tariff fuel surcharge exemption that has been expanded to more households up until the end of this year. Consumers are seeing relatively higher electricity bills from soaring temperatures and work-from-home policy and other seasonal factors. Last week, the government announced that households consuming 800 kilowatt-hour of power or less monthly will now be spared from surcharges under the automatic fuel adjustment. The exemption is previously provided only to those using under 600 kilowatt-hour each month. More importantly, Tenaga Nasional and the government are working on a more permanent solution for 2027 onwards to address elevated fuel price, CIMB Securities said. One possible approach could be differentiated rates versus the current uniform rate, and similar to how the imbalance cost pass-through, or ICPT, was previously implemented with residential users paying a lower rate against large-scale commercial users, the house noted. While there is no clarity on the new structure, the previous framework under ICPT mechanism allowed “cross subsidisation and potentially greater protection” for residential consumers and even small and medium enterprises, TA Securities added. Under the previous mechanism that was replaced in June 2025 with the automatic fuel adjustment system, the final tariff to be paid by consumers was adjusted every six months in the form of rebates or surcharges on top of the base tariff. title: HLB Meezani Account-i Offers Cash, Gold, And Cars In New Prize Draws
body: HLB Meezani Account-i holders stand a chance to win cash, gold bars, holiday packages, a Proton e.MAS 5, and a Porsche Cayenne in HLB Islamic’s second year of prize draws, which runs from 30 July 2026 to 29 July 2027. There are daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly draws, with minimum balances ranging from RM100 to RM60,000 depending on the prize. HLB Islamic announced this year’s prizes at a rewards ceremony in Kuala Lumpur on 29 September 2026, held to mark the account’s first year. The bank said 43% of those who opened the account in its first year were new HLB Islamic customers. The Minimum Balance For Each Prize Each prize has its own minimum balance, and you get one entry for every full multiple of that amount. For example, keeping RM1,000 in the account when the day ends gives 10 entries in the daily draw, since the minimum balance is RM100. For the weekly draw, you get one entry for every RM200. Keeping RM2,500 at the end of the week gives 12 entries, and the extra RM100 doesn’t count. For quarterly and yearly prizes, entries are counted from each month-end balance and added up until the draw. Keeping RM2,000 in the account at the end of each month for a three-month quarter, for example, gives three entries for the 10g gold bar draw. Since the monthly, quarterly, and yearly draws all use your month-end balance, withdrawing money on the last day of the month can reduce your entries for that month, even if you put the money back a few days later. Some Payments And Deposits Can Earn Extra Entries The monthly and quarterly prizes also offer extra entries if you’ve already met the minimum balance for the relevant prize. You can earn additional entries by making at least 10 eligible QR or online payments from the account in a month, or by depositing at least RM2,000 in a single transaction. Doing both in the same month earns one more combo entry. Making 10 payments earns extra entries for the RM500 cash and Touch ‘n Go prizes. A deposit of RM2,000 or more earns extra entries for every prize in the table except the Proton e.MAS 5, which only gets the combo entry when you do both in the same month. The daily, weekly, and yearly draws don’t offer extra entries. Win Limits And Claiming Your Prize You can win the daily prize once a week at most, and the weekly prize once every two weeks. If your name is selected for more than one monthly prize in the same month, you’ll only receive the highest-value prize. The same applies to the quarterly and yearly draws. To qualify for the draws, you need to actively use HLB Connect from the start of each draw period until any prize is handed over. Winners are selected within 30 working days after each draw period ends and notified through the HLB Connect app within 14 working days after that. You have 30 working days from the announcement to claim your prize, after which the bank may award it to another winner. Cash prizes are credited directly into the winner’s HLB Meezani Account-i. Winners are responsible for any taxes or fees related to their prizes, and HLB Islamic may publish winners’ names with part of their IC numbers concealed. Non-cash prizes are handed over within 90 working days. Winners will need their winning letter and IC to collect them. Prizes can’t be exchanged for cash or transferred to someone else. Opening An HLB Meezani Account-i The account is Shariah-compliant and open to individuals who live in Malaysia. You need RM100 to open it and RM50 to keep it open. The account currently has an indicative profit rate of 0.05% p.a., calculated daily and paid monthly, as of 30 September 2026. You can deposit or withdraw money through HLB Islamic branches, ATMs, cash deposit machines, and online channels. Because it’s an investment account rather than a savings account or fixed deposit, HLB Islamic states that the money and returns aren’t guaranteed and the account isn’t protected by Perbadanan Insurans Deposit Malaysia (PIDM). The prize draws come on top of the account’s profit rate, so look at both when deciding where to keep your money. You can also compare the latest savings account and fixed deposit rates on RinggitPlus. You can open the account at an HLB Islamic branch or book an appointment through the HLB Islamic website. The full rules are set out in the campaign’s terms and conditions [PDF]. Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for the latest money tips and updates. title: Maybank miliki sepenuhnya Etiqa selepas ambil alih baki 30.95% Ageas | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: KUALA LUMPUR 11 Sept – Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) melengkapkan cadangan pengambilalihan baki 30.95% kepentingan dalam Maybank Ageas Holdings Berhad (MAHB) dan menjadikan syarikat berkenaan sebagai anak syarikat milik penuh kumpulan perbankan itu. Maybank berkata, pengambilalihan tersebut disempurnakan selepas pihaknya menandatangani perjanjian pembelian saham (SPA) dengan Ageas Insurance International NV (Ageas) pada 8 September 2026. Cadangan pengambilalihan itu turut mendapat kelulusan kawal selia daripada Bank Negara Malaysia pada 1 September 2026 yang membolehkan proses pengambilalihan baki kepentingan tersebut diselesaikan. MAHB merupakan syarikat pegangan bagi perniagaan Etiqa di Malaysia dan Singapura yang menawarkan rangkaian produk insurans hayat dan am konvensional serta takaful keluarga dan am menerusi pelbagai saluran pengedaran. Presiden dan Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan Maybank, Datuk Sri Khairussaleh Ramli berkata langkah itu menjadi mercu tanda penting dalam usaha kumpulan memperkukuh aspirasi Etiqa untuk menjadi peneraju insurans dan takaful nasional. Kukuhkan Kedudukan Etiqa Di Asia Tenggara Menurut beliau, pemilikan penuh MAHB akan membantu Maybank memperkukuh kedudukan Etiqa sebagai peneraju insurans dan takaful, selain memperluas capaian kepada pangkalan pelanggan Maybank yang besar. Tambahnya, langkah itu juga selaras dengan aspirasi kumpulan untuk mengembangkan kedudukan Etiqa di Asia Tenggara serta membangunkan organisasi takaful bertaraf global menerusi strategi ROAR30. “Maybank akan memberi tumpuan kepada usaha memacu nilai kepada pelanggan di seluruh Asia Tenggara melalui tawaran kekayaan serantau, strategi jualan silang serta penyelesaian kewangan yang lebih bersepadu dan diperibadikan. ARTIKEL BERKAITAN: Maybank terima kelulusan BNM ambil alih baki pegangan Etiqa RM4.83 bilion “Pemilikan penuh MAHB turut membolehkan Maybank meningkatkan penciptaan nilai jangka panjang yang mampan melalui pengurusan modal yang lebih berkesan dalam kumpulan MAHB. “Pada masa sama, langkah tersebut dijangka meningkatkan keupayaan kumpulan untuk mengurus modal dengan lebih cekap di peringkat Maybank secara keseluruhan,” katanya dalam satu kenyataan hari ini. Peluang Pertumbuhan Insurans Dan Takaful Maybank berkata MAHB dijangka terus berada pada kedudukan kukuh untuk memanfaatkan peluang pertumbuhan dalam sektor insurans dan takaful. Kedudukan itu disokong oleh pangkalan pelanggan yang besar, rangkaian pengedaran Maybank yang menyeluruh serta permintaan pasaran yang semakin meningkat terhadap penyelesaian perlindungan yang bersepadu dan diperibadikan. Khairussaleh berkata, Maybank turut merakamkan penghargaan kepada Ageas atas kerjasama selama 25 tahun bersama kumpulan serta sumbangan syarikat itu dalam membangunkan francais Etiqa. Dengan pemilikan penuh tersebut, Maybank dan MAHB kini mempunyai keupayaan lebih tinggi untuk memacu inovasi produk, memperluas penembusan jualan insurans melalui bank serta memperkukuh tawaran takaful. Dalam masa sama, pemilikan penuh MAHB dijangka membantu kumpulan meningkatkan kecekapan modal dan operasi di seluruh Kumpulan Maybank, manakala jenama Etiqa akan terus dikekalkan sebagai salah satu jenama utama Maybank.

title: CIMB, Zetrix AI, Top Glove, Samaiden, Mesiniaga, Scientex, Dialog, Elridge Energy, Insights Analytics, SLGC
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 7): Here is a brief recap of some business news and corporate announcements that made the headlines on Tuesday: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people. A deal could value the business at as much as US$200 million (RM817 million). — CIMB considers selling Philippine business — Bloomberg Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314 million in unpaid remittances. In response to queries from Bursa Malaysia, the group reiterated that it had submitted a payment proposal to settle the arrears, and that the final sum and settlement terms remain subject to further discussions and formal agreement with authorities. — Zetrix says still finalising amount owed to JPJ after Loke reveals RM314m arrears Top Glove Corporation Bhd (KL:TOPGLOV) said labour shortage remains a primary constraint in scaling up production as it seeks to capture rising global demand following its best year since 2021. The group is targeting to raise annual running capacity by 8% to 78 billion pieces in the financial year ending Aug 31, 2027 (FY2027), from 72 billion in FY2026. The group’s net profit jumped nearly five times to RM157.63 million in the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 (4QFY2026) from RM34.83 million in the same quarter a year earlier. Revenue for the quarter surged 40% year-on-year to RM1.25 billion. A final dividend of 1.50 sen per share was also declared for FY2026 and payable on Dec 15. For the full FY2026, Top Glove’s net profit nearly tripled to RM307.96 million. Revenue increased 21% to RM4.23 billion as volume grew close to 30%. — Top Glove eyes higher output but says manpower remains key hurdle; Top Glove says ready for storms ahead as 4Q net profit jumps nearly five times Samaiden Group Bhd (KL:SAMAIDEN) said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99-megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238 million. Samaiden's wholly-owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation Bhd (KL:YTL). The project is among the LSS5+ projects approved by the Energy Commission in September 2025. — Samaiden reveals RM238 mil contract value for LSS5+ solar project Mesiniaga Bhd (KL:MSNIAGA) has won a RM32.3 million contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider’s earlier MyGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. The new extension, which takes effect from Oct 16, 2026, will run until Oct 15, 2028. — Mesiniaga wins two-year RM32.3m contract extension from Customs Dept Scientex Bhd (KL:SCIENTX) is acquiring 503 acres in Pulai, Johor, for RM580 million to boost the property developer’s land bank. The plan is to turn the 14 plots of land currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd (KL:LHI) into mixed development, the company said. However, it is too early to determine development value and other details, it noted. — Scientex to acquire 503 acres in Johor for RM580 mil Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Oct 5 that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand’s 25th Onshore Bid Round. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. — Dialog JV bags onshore O&G concession in Thailand Elridge Energy Holdings Bhd (KL:ELRIDGE) is investing RM45 million to venture into the manufacturing and sale of activated carbon business for use across water treatment, industrial purification and related filtration. This marks Elridge's move further downstream from its existing palm kernel shell biomass operations. Elridge said its wholly-owned subsidiary Lumeria Power Sdn Bhd (LP) had accepted a quotation from United Equipment Services (M) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition, installation and commissioning of six integrated activated carbon production chains for RM45 million in cash. — Elridge Energy invests RM45m to venture into activated carbon business Insights Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB), which mainly provides asset management systems to water utilities, has secured a RM14.44 million subcontract to construct a water treatment plant in Sarawak's Miri division. The contract involves the construction, operation and maintenance of the Suai water treatment plant, which will have a capacity of seven million litres per day, as part of a project aimed at addressing acute water supply shortages in the Suai area. The construction is scheduled to begin on Oct 13 and to be completed by April 10, 2027, followed by a 60-month operation and maintenance period. — Insights Analytics secures contract for Suai water treatment plant in Miri Building construction contractor SLGC Bhd (KL:SLG) ended its first trading day on the ACE Market below its initial public offering (IPO) price. title: Maybank Turned Its Cash Back Card Perks Into A Playground At Mid Valley
body: Last week, we dropped by Mid Valley Megamall to check out the Maybank Cash Back Mastercard Platinum showcase. Held at Centre Court from 23 to 27 September, the five-day event had a little bit of everything, from interactive activities to a closer look at the card’s features.  Five Stops To Explore The Card  The showcase was set up like a stamp-card journey. We picked up a journey card at the start and worked our way through five stations. The first four were More To Discover, Stream For More, More To Enjoy and More To Unwind. Once we had collected all four stamps, we could head to the final stop, Maybank Cafe, and redeem either a ZUS Coffee or a Krispy Kreme doughnut.  The activities at each station were also designed around the card’s benefits. One had a touchscreen game where you had to catch groceries in a basket, a playful take on the card’s 8% cash back on digital lifestyle spending. There were also photo spots with airplane window backdrops featuring destinations like Singapore, Thailand, Japan and South Korea, which are among the countries where the card charges no foreign exchange mark-up fee.  Visitors who applied for the card on-site could unlock three additional activities. These included a Flight Simulator and a Merchandise Redemption station with goodies such as a Maybank tumbler and Lilo & Stitch tote bag. Applicants could also try their luck at a giant Gashapon machine for prizes including a Nintendo Switch 2, Setel vouchers and Grab vouchers. title: Takaichi Pledges Fiscal Discipline as Japan's Debt Bill Rises
body: TOKYO (Oct 5): Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday pledged to "control" bond issuance and act swiftly against market turbulence, seeking to reassure investors worried about Japan's worsening public finances that have pushed up bond yields. She said the government would pursue fiscal sustainability even as it ramps up spending to bolster growth potential, including by reviewing existing tax breaks and subsidies. "Fiscal sustainability is obviously a prerequisite in pursuing our 'responsible and proactive' fiscal policy," Takaichi said in a policy speech to parliament. The remarks reflect mounting concern in Tokyo over rising Japanese government bond (JGB) yields, which would boost the cost of funding the premier's ambitious spending plans. The 30-year JGB yield hit a record high of 4.235% on Monday on jitters over the risk of increased debt issuance and inflation worries fuelled by the Middle East war. Japan's public debt, at roughly twice the size of its economy, is the largest in the developed world. Funding costs are climbing as the Bank of Japan raises interest rates and tapers bond purchases in an effort to wean the economy off decades of massive stimulus. Takaichi said the government will seek to draw in private investment in growth areas through "massive, long-term fiscal expenditure deployed in a well-planned, predictable manner." At the same time, it would keep a lid on annual bond issuance, calibrating borrowing to tax revenues, interest rates, debt-financing costs and economic and market developments, the premier said in the speech to an extraordinary parliament session that convened on Monday. "If the economy and markets make unexpected moves, we will scrutinise their impact and respond nimbly as needed," she added without elaborating. Fiscal policy is set to take centre stage in parliamentary debate in Japan as rising concerns over the fiscal health of advanced economies fuel a broader rise in global bond yields. The administration's immediate priority is passing legislation backing Takaichi's plan for a two-year tax cut on food items from next April, which sparked a bond selloff due to a lack of detail on how the revenue shortfall will be filled. The government is also preparing next year's budget, with ministries seeking record levels of spending. Separately, Takaichi said Tokyo will set aside multi-year funds for strategically important economic security initiatives. "We will implement policies steadily, get things done one by one, and communicate them carefully to the public and markets," Takaichi said. Keen to soothe market jitters, the administration has moved to dispel perceptions that its fiscal policy is reflationary or that it has leaned on the BOJ to refrain from hiking rates. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Saturday that the government has begun refining its messaging to reassure investors that Takaichi is not pursuing reflationary policies. But not all are on board. Former BOJ deputy governor Masazumi Wakatabe, a reflationist academic who is currently a private member of the government's key economic panel, said the recent rise in JGB yields was due to expectations of further BOJ rate hikes rather than concern over Japan's finances, minutes of the panel's recent meeting showed on Monday. Wakatabe also said the government had ultimate responsibility in guiding economic policy and stressed the need for close coordination between the BOJ and the administration on monetary policy, according to the minutes of the meeting which debated the central bank's rate-hike decision last month. title: DNB raises RM5.2bil from Islamic loan for next 5G phase
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, one of the largest syndicated loan facilities arranged for an unlisted Malaysian company. DNB said the financing comes as it prepares for the next phase of Malaysia's dual 5G network framework. The financing is expected to support the planned exit of the Ministry of Finance Inc (MoF Inc) as an ordinary shareholder, it said today. It will also facilitate the transition to equal ownership among DNB's mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders - CelcomDigi Bhd through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd - expected in early fourth quarter of this year. MoF Inc will retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and oversee key strategic matters. The RM5.2 billion facility also refinances DNB's government guarantee revolving credit facility, which expired on Sept 29. It provides the company with a long-term funding structure for its operations and network investments. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger. AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd were joint mandated lead arrangers. AmInvestment Bank also acted as financial adviser to DNB. The financing comes as DNB receives the full 100MHz of the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz (F0) spectrum and converts its entire 240MHz spectrum holding to a spectrum assignment. The assignment, issued by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, takes effect today. DNB said the expanded spectrum holding would increase network capacity, efficiency and performance, supporting faster speeds, lower latency and improved customer experience. It would also enable the deployment of technologies such as Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and artificial intelligence-driven network capabilities. DNB chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said the successful financing reflected confidence in the company's business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia's digital economy. "This financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate on its own, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and leverage our expanded spectrum assets," he said. Azman said DNB remained committed to providing digital infrastructure as Malaysia moved towards a dual network framework. "With strong financing, enhanced spectrum resources and a proven nationwide 5G platform, DNB is well positioned to support the government's AI Nation aspirations and help power Malaysia's next phase of digital growth," he said. DNB said the financing and spectrum assignment would strengthen its ability to improve network quality and resilience, cater to future demand and support Malaysia's digital economy ambitions.

title: Scheduling boo-boo: Malaysian hockey league matches originally set for Deepavali rescheduled - Twentytwo13
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Coaches of Premier League hockey teams scheduled to play on Deepavali day are happy they will now battle it out on different dates, as the Malaysian Hockey Confederation (MHC) repeats its 2018 scheduling boo-boo. Two matches – Terengganu Hockey Team against Armed Forces Hockey Team and TNB Thunderbolts versus Maybank – were originally scheduled for Nov 8, the day Deepavali is celebrated in Malaysia. However, the matches will now be rescheduled, much to the delight of TNB Thunderbolts and Terengganu Hockey Team. Mohd Harfizi Baharom of Terengganu said he had been informed that the match against the soldiers would now be played on Nov 9. “It is good that we will not be playing on such an auspicious day. It gives those celebrating the festival time to spend with their families,” Mohd Harfizi told Twentytwo13. “Several of our players have only just returned from the Asian Games. Unfortunately, there is a packed international calendar and the national team will be off to the Asian Champions Trophy from Oct 27 to Nov 5. “As such, having an extra day to prepare for the match against the Armed Forces is welcome. We are third in the standings, but have not given up hope of winning the title. One day can make a difference.” However, the new dates are not reflected on MHC’s website as of publication time. TNB Thunderbolts coach Nor Saiful Zaini, who is also the national junior coach, said he has yet to receive official notice of the new date. “I know it is not easy for MHC to juggle the calendar, but we shouldn’t play on Deepavali or any other religious festival. I am waiting for confirmation regarding the change of date,” said Nor Saiful. In 2018, the Razak Cup was initially scheduled from Nov 3-11, with Deepavali falling on Nov 6 that year. After protests from teams, especially Negeri Sembilan, which threatened to pull out of the tournament, MHC eventually brought forward the tournament to Oct 26-Nov 3. The repeat of the episode raised eyebrows, as those in charge of scheduling the league should have been fully aware of the festive seasons in the country. Meanwhile, Nor Saiful said he would have his hands full as the national juniors will compete in the Sultan of Johor Cup (Oct 17-24), followed by the Murugappa Gold Cup (Oct 25-Nov 4) in India. Nor Saiful was instrumental in recently guiding the national team to next year’s Junior World Cup. “I will need to juggle my team selection carefully, as we have to consider the league matches as well as the two major tournaments. “Some of the teams may be reluctant to release their junior players, but on the bright side, I have the chance to test more players in Johor and India,” he added.
