title: AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): While the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has been used extensively and relied upon in the last few years, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar cautioned for the need for human oversight in its usage.

Dusuki said there is no doubt that AI offers significant opportunities in various sectors.

For instance, he said, in healthcare, it can assist clinical judgement while in the corporate sphere, it can support decision-making, improve efficiency, and help professionals process increasingly complex information.

“But as our reliance on these systems grows, so, too, does the importance of understanding how they are used and how they are governed. We need to ask some very practical questions: How reliable is the information produced by an AI system? What are the limits of its capabilities? Who is responsible for checking its output?” he said.

He questioned what would happen when the AI system does not perform as expected.

“These are not merely questions about technology. They are questions of governance, professional responsibility, and human oversight. Increasingly, they may also have consequences for legal liability and insurance.

“For any institution adopting AI, it is therefore important to understand why the technology is being used, what risks may arise from its use, and what safeguards are necessary. Technology may assist professional judgement, but effective human oversight remains essential,” he reminded.

Dusuki was delivering his keynote address at the Inaugural Financial Lines Forum at a hotel here.

Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman and RHB Bank founder Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussin

Also present were Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman and RHB Bank founder Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussin, who delivered a special address, and former Federal Court judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali, former Chief Judge of Malaya Tan Sri Hasnah Mohamed Hashim, as well as former and current judges.

The AG said that while there are continuing issues in the usage of AI, there is a need to use it responsibly.

Dusuki said the use of AI requires engagement among those who develop the technology, those who deploy it, those who rely on it, and those who assess and manage the risks associated with its use.

Hence, he welcomed the organisation of such a forum like the Financial Lines Forum as it brings together legal professionals, healthcare practitioners, corporate leaders, insurers, brokers, and other stakeholders.

“We have an opportunity to learn from one another, to better understand the risks and opportunities before us, and to consider how our respective professions can respond responsibly to a rapidly changing environment.

“Ultimately, the question is not simply what artificial intelligence can do. The more important question is, how we, as professionals, choose to use it responsibly,” he added.

The one-day forum gathers medical experts, insurers, lawyers, and judges in exchanging views on medical negligence, governance, and AI.

title: Warga Palestin diculik: Waran tangkap terhadap tertuduh ketujuh | Sinar Harian
body: Warga Palestin diculik: Waran tangkap terhadap tertuduh ketujuh KUALA LUMPUR – Mahkamah Tinggi di sini pada Jumaat mengeluarkan waran tangkap terhadap seorang daripada lapan tertuduh dalam kes penculikan seorang lelaki warga Palestin pada 2022. Hakim, Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin mengeluarkan perintah itu terhadap Muhammad Iqmal Abdul Rahis, 31, selepas tertuduh tidak hadir pada prosiding kes berkenaan. Ketika pengurusan kes, penjamin tertuduh memaklumkan bahawa, usaha menjejaki Muhammad Iqmal termasuk pergi ke rumahnya di kawasan ladang kelapa sawit telah dilakukan sebelum ini. “Saya pergi ke kampungnya di Tanjung Sepat, tetapi adik-beradik dia kata tidak jumpa,” katanya. Sementara itu, Timbalan Pendakwa Raya, Zaileen Nadia Zubir berkata, pihak pendakwaan juga sudah berusaha mengesan tertuduh ketujuh itu sejak 11 September lalu. Menurutnya, pihak berkuasa turut pergi ke Tanjung Sepat, Banting, Kuala Langan dan bertanyakan mengenai keberadaan tertuduh kepada bapanya. “Bapa tertuduh memberitahu lelaki berkenaan tidak balik kampung sejak Januari lalu dan pihak berkuasa masih berusaha mengesan tertuduh,” katanya. Susulan itu, Hakim, Mohd Arief Emran mengeluarkan waran tangkap terhadap Muhammad Iqmal. Mahkamah turut memerintahkan wang jaminan sebanyak RM50,000 dikembalikan kepada penjamin selepas mengambil kira usaha yang dilakukan bagi mengesan tertuduh. Dalam prosiding itu, Muhammad Iqmal diwakili peguam, Goh Cia Yee. Sebelum ini, mahkamah menetapkan perbicaraan kes berkenaan ditetapkan pada 12 hingga 15, 19 hingga 23 dan 26 hingga 29 October. Pada Oktober 2022, seramai 13 lelaki dan seorang wanita didakwa di Mahkamah Majistret di sini atas pertuduhan menculik warga Palestin, Omar Z M Albelbaisy Raeda, 35, bagi mendapatkan ganjaran berupa rahsia maklumat berkaitan perisian menggodam telefon bimbit. Mereka ialah Edy Ko’im Said, 46, Mohamad Norakmal Hassan, 47, Dody Junaidi, 48, Tengku Arif Bongsu Tengku Hamid, 45, Mohamad Naziree Mustapha, 45, Faizull Hardey Mohd Isa, 46, Muhammad Iqmal, Mohamad Sufian Saly, 29, Muhammad Al Hatim Mohd Fauzi, 29, Nidarahayu Zainal, 40, Raibafie Amdan, 45, Mohd Zaidi Mohd Zain, 60, Mohd Azwan Jamaludin 55, dan Tengku Hazarul Ismail Tengku Hamid, 55. Kesalahan itu didakwa dilakukan di Jalan Mayang, di sini, pada jam 10.40 malam 28 September 2022. Pertuduhan dibuat mengikut Seksyen 3 Akta Penculikan 1961 dibaca bersama Seksyen 34 Kanun Keseksaan yang memperuntukkan hukuman penjara antara 30 hingga 40 tahun serta sebatan, jika sabit kesalahan. Pada 20 Oktober 2023, Tengku Arif Bongsu bersama pasangan suami isteri, Nidarahayu dan Raibafie turut didakwa atas 19 pertuduhan pengubahan wang haram berjumlah lebih RM250,000. Bagi pertuduhan pertama hingga keempat, Nidarahayu didakwa melupuskan wang RM20,650.86 hasil aktiviti haram daripada akaun simpanannya di CIMB Bank ke dua akaun bank lain di CIMB Bank dan Maybank Islamic Berhad di Cawangan Taman Maluri, antara 15 September hingga 3 Oktober 2022. Dia turut berdepan 13 pertuduhan memindahkan wang RM184,985.46 ke dalam akaun empat syarikat dan lapan individu, juga hasil aktiviti haram, antara 15 September hingga 2 Oktober tahun sama. Raibafie dan Tengku Arif Bongsu masing-masing didakwa menerima RM30,350 dan RM25,000 daripada dua akaun bank milik Nidarahayu serta sebuah syarikat, di CIMB Bank Cawangan Jalan Bukit Bintang dan Taman Mutiara, Cheras antara 29 September hingga 2 Oktober 2022. Pertuduhan dibuat mengikut Seksyen 4(1)(b) Akta Pencegahan Pengubahan Wang Haram, Pencegahan Pembiayaan Keganasan dan Hasil daripada Aktiviti Haram 2001 yang membawa hukuman penjara maksimum 15 tahun dan denda lima kali ganda nilai aktiviti haram atau RM5 juta, yang mana lebih tinggi, jika sabit kesalahan. Pada 10 Julai 2025, enam lelaki dihukum penjara lima tahun oleh Mahkamah Tinggi di sini selepas mengaku bersalah atas pertuduhan pilihan melarikan dan mengurung seorang lelaki Palestin itu. Hakim, K Muniandy yang kini hakim Mahkamah Rayuan di Putrajaya, menjatuhkan hukuman itu terhadap Mohamad Norakmal, Mohd Azwan, Dody, Mohamad Sufian, Tengku Hazarul Ismail dan Muhammad Al Hatim. Mengikut pertuduhan, mereka didakwa melarikan mangsa secara paksa terhadap lelaki Palestine sama dengan dikurung secara salah dan rahsia di Jalan Mayang, Dang Wangi di sini pada jam 10.40 malam, 28 September 2022. Kesemua tertuduh didakwa mengikut Seksyen 365 Kanun Keseksaan dan dibaca bersama Seksyen 34 akta sama yang membawa hukuman penjara sehingga tujuh tahun dan boleh dikenakan denda. Mengikut fakta kes, mangsa dilarikan dan dikurung di sebuah chalet di Hulu Langat. title: DNB secures RM5.2 bil for next phase of 5G growth, MOF retains special share
body: Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion financing exercise as it moves into the next phase of Malaysia’s 5G development. The financing comes as the nation’s first 5G network has secured a new long-term spectrum assignment, while the government (via MOF Inc) will exit as an ordinary shareholder. CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL are expected to hold equal ownership in DNB. Transition is expected to be completed in early Q4 2026, however, MOF Inc. will retain a special share. DNB completes RM5.2 billion financing DNB said it has completed a RM5.2 billion Syndicated Islamic Term Financing exercise, which it described as among the largest syndicated loan facilities ever arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia. Maybank Investment Bank acted as Mandated Lead Arranger, Bookrunner and Coordinating Arranger, while AmInvestment Bank, CIMB Islamic Bank, RHB Islamic Bank and United Overseas Bank Malaysia were Joint Mandated Lead Arrangers. AmInvestment Bank also acted as financial adviser to DNB. The financing will also be used to refinance DNB’s Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on 29 September 2026. According to DNB, the new financing provides a sustainable long-term funding structure to support its future growth. The financing is also expected to reduce the need for additional equity funding from DNB’s mobile network operator shareholders, based on DNB’s current regulatory commitments and funding requirements. DNB CEO Datuk Azman Ismail said, “The successful completion of this RM5.2 billion financing exercise marks a significant milestone for DNB and reflects strong confidence in our business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia’s digital economy. This financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate on its own, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and leverage our expanded spectrum assets.” He added, “As Malaysia progresses under the dual network framework, DNB remains committed to providing world-class digital infrastructure that supports our shareholders, customers, enterprises and government agencies. With strong financing, enhanced spectrum resources and a proven nationwide 5G platform, DNB is well positioned to support the Government’s AI Nation aspirations and help power Malaysia’s next phase of digital growth.” DNB gets 15-year 5G spectrum certainty DNB has also received the full 100MHz block in the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz band, known as F0, while its entire 240MHz spectrum holding has been converted from Apparatus Assignment (AA) into Spectrum Assignment (SA). The Spectrum Assignment for a 15-year period awarded by the MCMC provides greater long-term certainty over spectrum availability and it takes effect from 1 October 2026. By securing 200MHz of the contiguous mid-band spectrum (3.3 to 3.5GHz), DNB has a stronger foundation to modernise the network, expand indoor building solutions, enhance coverage and maximise spectrum utilisation. In addition, DNB also has 2x 20Hz blocks of the low band spectrum with 703MHz to 723MHz and 758Hz to 778MHz. DNB said its spectrum holdings will also support higher network capacity and efficiency, as well as technologies including Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities. MOF to retain special share in DNB While the recent financing facilitates MOF Inc.’s planned exit as an ordinary shareholder of DNB, the government via MOF Inc will continue to retain a special share in the company. According to DNB, the special share will safeguard national interests and ensure continued stewardship over key strategic matters. Following the share transfer, the mobile network operator shareholders would assume a greater role in jointly steering DNB’s strategic and operational priorities. In a separate statement issued by CelcomDigi, the telco says it will bring its scale, nationwide network assets and more than 30 years of telecommunications experience to support DNB. This includes leveraging on existing infrastructure, sites and capabilities to drive cost efficiencies, support coverage expansion and accelerate indoor 5G deployment.

title: Stock Focus
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL: CIMB) could potentially raise its RM2 billion capital return commitment to increase the chances of its share buyback programme garnering investor acceptance, according to MBSB Research.  A higher capital-return commitment could help offset potential disappointment among investors who are expecting a larger portion of the RM2 billion to be returned via special dividends, the research house said.  “To increase its chances of success, we think there is a likelihood of CIMB positively revising to the RM2.0 billion figure, and that CIMB is confident enough on its ability to garner sufficient capital before signalling to the market via share buybacks,” MBSB Research said in a note on Thursday.  “We would not put it past CIMB’s management to pull off such a manoeuvre — they’ve surprised us positively multiple times in the past,” it added.  MBSB Research noted that share buybacks have historically not been successful in Malaysia. CIMB’s share buybacks make up a portion of its RM2 billion capital return scheme, of which RM700 million has already been returned via special dividends.  The primary purpose of the share buybacks is for CIMB to further drive its earnings per share, return on equity (ROE) and dividend per share figures, MBSB Research noted, particularly as the bank is slightly behind on its ROE target for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026).  The research house noted CIMB has been buying back shares every day, tallying up to 20.76 million shares for RM163 million since Sept 21 thus far.  Who could follow CIMB?  CIMB’s share buyback programme is also being watched for its potential implications on other banks, according to MBSB Research.  The research house described the programme as the first major share buyback scheme by a Malaysian bank for capital management purposes in many years, and said a successful outcome could encourage other large banks to consider similar measures.  It listed Public Bank Bhd (KL: PBBANK) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL: RHBBANK) as possible candidates.  Public Bank, it noted, has already received shareholder approval for a share buyback of up to 10% of its shares, although it has not done any yet. Its management has maintained that this is a capital optimisation option rather than a set path they want to go down, the research house added.  RHB Bank, meanwhile, has high capital ratios and historically releases excess capital via larger payouts in the fourth quarter, MBSB Research noted. It is currently preparing a new capital release plan, which is scheduled to be announced by the first quarter of FY2027, the research house added.  MBSB Research maintained its “buy” call on CIMB but with a lower target price of RM9.20 from RM9.29, based on an unchanged FY2027 forecast price-to-book value of 1.33 times.  At the time of writing, shares of CIMB were down three sen or 0.39% at RM7.76, valuing the lender at RM84 billion.

title: Laws alone will not shield our children online
body: AI and the relentless subscription to social media pose many new challenges to ordinary people, not just in Malaysia but around the world. The government deserves credit for introducing laws to safeguard the young from AI manipulation and social media abuse. New laws, new duties The Online Safety Act 2025 came into force on 1 January. This landmark law gives the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) sweeping powers to enforce safety standards on digital services. The laws aim to protect children from AI-generated child sexual abuse material, deepfakes, online grooming and voice cloning. They also shift responsibility from parents as watchdogs to digital platforms, which must have strict built-in accountability features. The Child Protection Code and the Risk Mitigation Code came into force on 1 June. They require platforms to build in ‘child-by-design’ safeguards. Platforms must also label AI-generated synthetic media, such as deepfakes, so young users and parents can spot manipulative or misleading content. Those that do not comply face fines of up to RM10m. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member There are also mandatory age-verification checks to stop children under 16 from registering for social media or high-risk content accounts. The Cybercrimes Bill 2026, passed in July, targets synthetic and AI-generated threats to children. Section 23 criminalises the use of deepfake technology to produce and spread harmful, malicious material. Section 24 outlaws the sharing of non-consensual intimate images. This extends protection to minors from AI that digitally alters school photos and similar images. The government has also set out seven key principles for responsible AI, focusing on reliability, safety, control, privacy and data security. These help protect children from AI tools that track data and use biased algorithms. The aim is a transparent, ethical system that acts as a shield for our most vulnerable – our children. Awareness must follow Other initiatives due in the months ahead include national digital literacy programmes. These aim to build resilience in children rather than rely on bans. The laws will need strong public awareness campaigns. They must reach not only consumers but also the AI back-end developers and social media programmers. Other ministries, including education and trade and economics, will need to work with the MCMC. Each should run campaigns covering the parts of the laws that apply to them. Only then can we hope for the vigilance needed to make these laws work. The video above, in which a mother describes how she lost her teenage son to the dangers of AI and social media, should send shivers down the spine. It is also a timely reminder to governments, leaders, parents, teachers and anyone else who helps protect the digital lives of children. However, given Malaysia’s track record of enthusiastic, knee-jerk reactions to new ideas that are quickly forgotten, there is much to worry about. title: Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi sejajar sentimen positif serantau
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi hari ini, sejajar dengan peningkatan dalam kebanyakan pasaran utama Asia susulan kenaikan saham teknologi di Wall Street dalam tempoh semalaman, walaupun hasil bon Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang tinggi terus mengehadkan minat terhadap risiko. Pada 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 1.60 mata kepada 1,633.35 berbanding 1,631.75 semasa ditutup pada Isnin. Indeks petunjuk pasaran itu yang dibuka 4.63 mata lebih tinggi kepada 1,636.38, bergerak antara 1,632.77 dan 1,641.20 sepanjang sesi dagangan. Dalam pasaran secara menyeluruh, kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 667 berbanding 456 manakala 551 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,108 tidak diniagakan dan 13 yang lain digantung dagangan. Jumlah dagangan susut kepada 4.18 bilion unit bernilai RM2.95 bilion berbanding 4.78 bilion unit bernilai RM2.89 bilion semalam. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng, berkata hasil bon Perbendaharaan AS dalam tempoh 10 tahun mencecah 5.349 peratus, paras tertinggi sejak 2002 manakala hasil bon 30 tahun meningkat seketika kepada 5.703 peratus. Semasa ditutup pada Isnin, S&P 500 meningkat 0.66 peratus kepada 7,773.95 mata manakala Indeks Komposit Nasdaq naik 1.05 peratus kepada 27,477.31 mata. "Dari sudut positif, harga minyak mentah Brent menyusut di bawah AS$100 setong apabila eksport Asia Barat yang kekal kukuh serta pelepasan stok simpanan kecemasan oleh negara-negara Kumpulan Tujuh (G7) membantu mengurangkan kebimbangan terhadap bekalan," katanya kepada Bernama. Menurutnya di dalam negara, minat belian dapat dilihat dalam saham telekomunikasi dan berkaitan komoditi manakala aktiviti dagangan turut meluas kepada beberapa kaunter teknologi bermodal kecil, tenaga dan perladangan. "Kami yakin bahawa saham mewah terpilih boleh terus menarik aktiviti pembelian saham ketika harga rendah susulan pembetulan yang ketara minggu lalu. Bagaimanapun, ketiadaan pembelian susulan sepanjang tiga sesi dagangan lepas menunjukkan pelabur terus berwaspada, dengan jualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing dan hasil bon yang tinggi dijangka mengehadkan kadar pemulihan," katanya. Sementara itu, Thong berkata, penurunan harga minyak mentah dan harapan mengenai Belanjawan 2027 dijangka memberikan sedikit sokongan kepada sentimen. "Belanjawan akan dibentangkan pada Jumaat, dengan sektor strategik termasuk semikonduktor, kecerdasan buatan, pendigitalan, peralihan tenaga, farmaseutikal, logistik dan aeroangkasa antara bidang yang diberi tumpuan oleh kerajaan," katanya. Bagi tempoh yang masih berbaki minggu ini, beliau menjangkakan indeks petunjuk pasaran itu kekal dalam fasa konsolidasi dengan kecenderungan untuk pulih secara sederhana apabila situasi terlebih jual memberikan sedikit sokongan kepada pasaran daripada penurunan selanjutnya. "Bagaimanapun, pemulihan yang lebih kukuh mungkin memerlukan pemangkin baharu, dengan Belanjawan 2027, aliran dana asing, hasil bon dan perkembangan geopolitik kekal sebagai faktor utama untuk diberikan perhatian. "Kami mengekalkan julat dagangan FBM KLCI pada 1,620 hingga 1,650 mata bagi minggu ini," katanya. Antara saham wajaran tinggi, IHH Healthcare meningkat 15 sen kepada RM7.91 manakala Maybank dan CIMB masing-masing susut tiga sen kepada RM9.97 dan RM7.70. Public Bank turun empat sen kepada RM4.67 manakala Tenaga Nasional susut 10 sen kepada RM12.90. Bagi saham aktif, Zetrix AI dan Supermax masing-masing meningkat 2.5 sen kepada sembilan sen dan 46 sen, Top Glove menokok sembilan sen kepada 87.5 sen, V.S Industry naik satu sen kepada 33 sen manakala SLGC yang baru disenaraikan di Pasaran ACE susut tiga sen kepada 25 sen. Antara kaunter paling untung, Malaysian Pacific Industries meningkat RM1.56 kepada RM44.96, Nestle naik RM1.26 kepada RM91.26, Pentamaster melonjak 64 sen kepada RM6.08, Mi Technovation menokok 59 sen kepada RM6.00 manakala Kuala Lumpur Kepong naik 46 sen kepada RM21.32. Kaunter paling rugi diterajui Dutch Lady Milk Industries yang susut 30 sen kepada RM29.70, Allianz turun 18 sen kepada RM20.62, TIME dotCom susut 16 sen kepada RM5.45 manakala Mega First Corporation dan Ayer Holdings masing-masing rendah 15 sen kepada RM2.85 dan RM7.55. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 melonjak 190.62 mata kepada 17,734.11, Indeks FBM Emas meningkat 42.52 mata kepada 12,232.87, Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 42.40 mata kepada 12,015.78, Indeks FBM Emas Syariah meningkat 89.97 mata kepada 12,158.98 manakala Indeks FBM ACE melonjak 52.31 mata kepada 5,658.92. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian meningkat 1.44 mata kepada 180.41 namun Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan susut 72.14 mata kepada 19,068.0. Indeks Tenaga pula meningkat 10.78 mata kepada 840.72 manakala Indeks Perladangan melonjak 111.14 mata kepada 9,042.17. title: AHB KEKALKAN AGIHAN PENDAPATAN LIMA SEN SEUNIT BAGI TAHUN KEWANGAN 2026 – Gerbangpost.com
body: KUALA LUMPUR,. Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan agihan pendapatan sebanyak lima sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 Sept 2026, yang KUALA LUMPUR,. Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan agihan pendapatan sebanyak lima sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 Sept 2026, yang memberi manfaat kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB) bersama pengurus dananya, PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM), berkata agihan pendapatan akhir bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 Sept 2026 adalah sebanyak 2.1 sen seunit, dengan tambahan agihan bonus sebanyak 0.4 sen seunit yang diisytiharkan PHB selaku penaja dana itu. “Edaran bonus itu akan diberikan bagi 1,000,000 unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit. Dengan mengambil kira agihan pendapatan interim sebanyak 2.5 sen seunit yang diisytiharkan pada April 2026, jumlah keseluruhan agihan pendapatan AHB bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 2026 adalah lima sen seunit,” menurut kenyataan itu. PHB berkata sebanyak RM120.13 juta akan diagihkan pada pusingan akhir, menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan agihan tahunan sebanyak RM236.41 juta. Pengarah Urusan kumpulan PHB Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad berkata agihan pendapatan bagi setahun penuh itu mencerminkan daya tahan AHB yang berterusan serta kekuatan portfolio hartanah asasnya, disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset dan pelaburan yang berdisiplin oleh PHB. “Prestasi AHB tahun ini membuktikan komitmen kami untuk terus memberikan pulangan yang kompetitif kepada pemegang unit. “Pada masa sama, kami kekal memberi tumpuan kepada usaha memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan pelabur Bumiputera menerusi pengurusan modal yang berhemat, strategi pelaburan yang dinamik serta pengoptimuman portfolio yang berterusan bagi memastikan pertumbuhan yang mampan danpenciptaan nilai jangka panjang,” katanya. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PHBAM Zulkifli Ishak berkata pengurus dana itu kekal fokus menguruskan AHB secara bertanggungjawab bagi memastikan dana berkenaan terus menjadi pilihan pelaburan yang mudah diakses oleh pelabur Bumiputera. PHB berkata agihan pendapatan itu akan dibayar dalam bentuk unit AHB yang dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun AHB pemegang unit selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Okt 2026. Agihan tersebut akan dilaburkan semula secara automatik, sekali gus membolehkan pemegang unit menambah pegangan unit serta berpotensi menikmati kesan pengkompaunan dalam jangka panjang. “Pelabur Bumiputera yang ingin melanggan AHB boleh berbuat demikian pada harga tetap RM1 seunit, dengan pelaburan minimum RM100 dan maksimum RM1 juta. “Langganan boleh dibuat melalui cawangan pengedar yang sah di seluruh negara, iaitu Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), AmBank Bhd, AmBank Islamic Bhd, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd dan Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd,” katanya. — BERNAMA

title: Dialog JV Bags Onshore O&G Concession in Thailand
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Monday (Oct 5) that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand’s 25th Onshore Bid Round, according to Dialog's Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. The development of L8/66 carries a minimum work commitment of US$14.3 million (RM58.4 million). The award remains subject to the finalisation and execution of the concession agreement and the fulfilment of its conditions precedent, with physical work expected to begin immediately after the agreement is signed. POES is a joint venture between Dialog’s wholly-owned Pan Orient Petroleum Pte Ltd and Thailand-based Sea Oil Energy Ltd, which holds the remaining 49.99%. Dialog, through POES, already operates the producing L53/48 onshore concession in Thailand, which is adjacent to the L8/66 block. L8/66 was previously part of the L53/48 concession before being relinquished to the Thai government under concession terms requiring portions of undeveloped acreage to be surrendered over time. Dialog said the new block has similar geological characteristics to L53/48 and gives POES access to additional acreage surrounding its existing producing fields. “The award of Concession L8/66 to POES further strengthens Dialog’s upstream portfolio and creates operational synergies by leveraging on the group’s integrated technical services across its diversified business model,” the company said. "Dialog will remain focused and steadfast in the pursuit of diversification across the upstream, midstream and downstream energy sector as well as the sustainable and renewable sector, to strategically position the group to weather different economic and oil price cycles, which is in line with the group's strategy of generating long term recurring income," it added. For the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY2026), Dialog’s net profit surged 95.4% to RM593.55 million from RM303.83 million a year earlier, as revenue grew 15.3% to RM2.88 billion from RM2.5 billion. The stronger FY2026 performance was driven by positive contributions across the group’s businesses, particularly its Malaysian operations, while its international businesses also recorded higher profit contributions on increased sales of specialist products and services. Dialog proposed a final dividend of three sen per share, bringing its total dividend for FY2026 to 4.7 sen per share or about RM265.93 million. Dialog shares closed two sen or 1.08% higher at RM1.87 on Tuesday, valuing the group at RM10.56 billion. Year to date, the counter has gained over 6%. title: High Court to rule Oct 23 on Maritime Network’s bid to keep RHB accounts open
body:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court yesterday fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit.

Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P. Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank’s counsel, Gan Khong Aik.

Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts.

He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care.

Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer was that of debtor and creditor.

In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company’s application for a full injunction.

According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005.

On Oct 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated Oct 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines.

The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines had allegedly been breached.

The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025.

The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application.

The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its Minimum Due Diligence guidelines governing foreign exchange transactions to the company within 45 days.

Maritime Network further alleged that the bank’s vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself.

The company asserted that this conduct amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights.

It also claimed that the bank’s conduct demonstrated an intention to oppress rather than protect its legitimate banking interests.

title: RHB online banking to drop support for older browsers from Oct 31
body: PETALING JAYA: RHB Bank has announced that its online banking platform will stop supporting older, outdated browsers from Oct 31. These outdated browsers will not be able to access the platform after this date. In a notice on its website, the bank says the change is intended to provide a safer and more secure banking experience for customers. It adds that this is due to older browsers no longer receiving security updates from their respective providers. The bank has set the minimum versions for five browsers, consisting of Google Chrome (V149 and above), Microsoft Edge (V149 and above), Mozilla Firefox (V151 and above), Opera (V130 and above), and Apple Safari (V18 and above). No action is needed if the browser is already on a newer version. For customers unable to update their browser to a newer version, RHB Bank advises them to use the RHB Mobile Banking App, available on both the Google Play Store and Apple App Store.

title: PETRONAS to Submit First in Sarawak Oil Rights Dispute, But Only Full FC Bench Can Decide on Preliminary Issues Hearing
body: PUTRAJAYA (Oct 1): A Federal Court judge has decided that only a full bench can decide on a preliminary issue raised by the Sarawak government in the dispute with PETRONAS over who has control over the oil in the state. Federal Court judge Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang on Thursday declined to make a ruling on the hearing of the preliminary issue, saying that the full Federal Court bench that will hear the separate PETRONAS and Sarawak government petitions should decide on the matter. The full bench hearing is scheduled for Jan 25 next year. Sarawak wants the preliminary issue of the legality of the colonial-era Order In Council 1954 (OIC) law to be heard before PETRONAS' petition about the competence of 10 Sarawak laws. The state government asserts that the OIC extends Sarawak's maritime borders beyond what is set in federal law and includes the continental shelf. The legal wrangle over who has control over oil found in Sarawak was sparked by the founding of state oil company Petros in 2016. Earlier this year, PETRONAS filed its petition to challenge the competency of 10 Sarawak laws on Jan 12, while Sarawak filed its challenge on three federal laws on Feb 23. Rhodzariah on Thursday said it would be improper for her to decide on the preliminary issue as the two cases are not consolidated, and the full bench might rule differently than her. However, Rhodzariah ruled that with regard to the submission of substantive arguments (the main matter of the case), based on the sequence of the filing of the petitions, PETRONAS would orally submit the issues raised in its petition first, and Sarawak after that. “This is based on the normal practice that the first petition filed first would be heard first, and subsequently the other. The fact that PETRONAS obtained leave (permission) from the Federal Court only on March 16 was not a consideration,” she ruled after a short 20-minute recess. The judge also asked parties (PETRONAS, the Sarawak government, and the federal government) to write in their applications to Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh, as they sought a panel of nine to 11 judges at the apex court constitutional hearing scheduled for five days beginning Jan 25 next year. A Federal Court bench usually comprises three or five judges. A full bench is convened for cases of extraordinary weight. Datuk Dr Cyrus Das appearing for PETRONAS, senior federal counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly @ Arwi, and Sarawak senior state counsel Mohd Adzrul Azlan indicated they would do so. Mohd Adzrul told the court that Sarawak would possibly indicate one or two judges who should not hear the matter. It is to be noted that besides the top-four judges — the Chief Justice, President of the Court of Appeal Datuk Seri Abu Bakar Jais, Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah, and Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi — there are 11 other apex court judges. PETRONAS is challenging the competency of the Sarawak assembly in enacting 10 laws which it says encroaches on federal government powers as set out in the Constitution's the Federal List. Chief among them is the OIC law, which extends Sarawak’s offshore borders beyond what is set by the federal government and international treaties. The OIC sets Sarawak’s offshore border to beyond three nautical miles from its shores and includes its continental shelf. The other state legislations being challenged by PETRONAS include the Environment (Reduction of Greenhouse Gas Emission) Ordinance 2023 and the Sarawak Oil Mining Ordinance 1958. Meanwhile, Sarawak is challenges three federal laws: the Petroleum Development Act 1974, the Continental Shelf Act 1966 and the Petroleum Mining Act 1966. Last week, parties indicated before Rhodzariah that they want their petitions to be heard separately and not be consolidated, but they do not agree on the sequence. The parties indicated that they do not mind the same judges hearing the petitions. On Thursday, parties indicated before Rhodzariah that they still disagree on which petition should be heard first. Cyrus said PETRONAS’ petition should be first because it was filed first. The senior lawyer said that since the Sarawak government had raised the OIC law in its defence, this indicates that it is a pre-emptive move by the state for it to be heard at the outset. “This court should not entertain such pre-emptive moves. Furthermore, the Federal Government is supporting PETRONAS that the company should submit first,” he said. Mohd Adzrul told Rhodzariah that since the OIC is central to PETRONAS’ argument, thus by ease of reference, the Sarawak petition should be heard first. “It is important to note that the OIC was never revoked or amended, and remains a part of the state law. There is a need for the apex court to decide the status of the OIC. Our petition should take precedence, because the dispute is between the state and the federal government as a party. “The court would have to decide whether it has original jurisdiction to touch on the OIC. This is the reason why we say the Sarawak government should be allowed to submit first, so that the submissions could be dealt with in a structured manner,” he said. Ahmad Hanir said the federal government supports PETRONAS’ application to submit first, as this a federal-state dispute and there is no need for the apex court to hear or decide on the preliminary issue. Following Rhodzariah’s decision on not deciding on Sarawak's preliminary issue, Mohd Adzrul said the state would apply for it be heard first. “The application will be filed within 14 days from today (Thursday),” he said, adding that they would file their written submissions in accordance with the agreed directions on Jan 11, and reply on Jan 18. Besides Das, Khoo Guan Huat, Datuk Azian Abd Aziz, Grace Teoh Wei Shan, Ahmad Faiz Razali, Khoo Yuan Ping and Alex Ngu appeared for PETRONAS. For Sarawak, besides Mohd Adzrul, the state is represented by Sarawak counsel Richard Tie Sing Wan and Felicity Sharmela Thomas. In addition to Ahmad Hanir, federal counsel Imtiyaz Wizni Aufa Othman represented the federal government. title: Maybank Falls Below RM10 for First Time in Nine Months as Rising Bond Yields Hurt Banking Stocks
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields. Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. Investors may also demand higher returns on corporate bonds, affecting appetite for new issuances. That would weigh on banks’ near term non-interest income as well as their capital ratios, Affin Hwang Investment Bank flagged in a note on Thursday. Maybank, the country’s top bank in terms of assets, fell for the third straight day and closed down 0.4% at RM9.95. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) and Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL:HLBANK) each declined over 1%. The Bursa Malaysia Financial Services Index, which also tracks non-bank firms such as insurers and stockbrokers, fell to its lowest level in 10 months. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating. A growing number of economists expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the overnight policy rate in November during the final scheduled monetary policy review for the year. Rising yields tend to lead to higher corporate bond yields, which also tie-in to capital raising decisions both for banks and other corporates and, subsequently, fee income to the banks, Affin Hwang said. Maybank and Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (KL:ABMB) have on their books the longest bond duration — the length of time for a bond to repay its cost in cash flows while also being a measure of sensitivity to changes in interest rates — according to the research house’s analysis. Public Bank Bhd (KL:PBBANK) and Hong Leong Bank, meanwhile, have the shortest duration. In terms of capital ratios, Maybank, RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) and CIMB could see the largest drops, while Public Bank and Hong Leong Bank would see the least due to their portfolios’ shorter duration, the house added. title: CIMB Completes Malaysia’s First Tokenised Sukuk Settlement Using Tokenised Deposits
body: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd has completed a pilot to test the settlement of tokenised sukuk using tokenised deposits in a controlled environment, paving the way for broader applications enabled by blockchain technology. These potential applications include instant, or atomic, settlement for cross-border transactions, as well as the democratisation of investment assets — such as enabling bonds to be sold in smaller amounts that retail investors can more easily afford. The pilot was carried out through CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd in connection with a RM1.68 billion issuance under CIMB Islamic’s existing RM10 billion senior sukuk wakalah programme, with tenors of five, seven, 10 and 15 years. Of the total issuance, RM1.38 billion was issued in tokenised form and subscribed to by 12 institutional investors, while the remaining RM300 million was issued as a traditional sukuk. The order book was covered 1.73 times, with the pricing date set at Aug 19 and settlement completed on Aug 27, according to Sylvia Wong, regional head of tokenisation at CIMB Group Wholesale Banking. The key distinction between CIMB’s pilot and an earlier pilot conducted by Khazanah Nasional Bhd lies in how settlement occurred. CIMB’s pilot involved settling both the tokenised sukuk and tokenised deposits, meaning the financial asset and the cash were both settled on-chain — though the tokens mirror legal records that continue to exist within the traditional system. A tokenised deposit refers to a bank deposit recorded as a digital token on a blockchain, effectively representing commercial bank money in digital form. In contrast, Khazanah’s tokenised sukuk, which settled in mid-May, was paid for using fiat currency, or the ringgit, through traditional payment rails rather than blockchain. In that case, only the financial asset was settled on-chain, while the cash portion moved through conventional channels. “For our pilot, we created tokenised deposits to settle the tokenised sukuk, so both of these settlements are on the blockchain,” Wong said, adding that the blockchain used for the settlement is called CIMB Blockchain Connect. The digital asset custodian (DAC) involved in the pilot — the entity responsible for safeguarding clients’ tokenised assets — is not among the two DACs currently registered with the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC). “For this pilot, we cleared with the SC that a DAC licence is not required. We just need the ability to custodise these assets and the deposits,” Wong said during a press conference. What It Means for Ordinary People Wong explained that the central feature of the pilot is atomic settlement, where a buyer’s money and a seller’s asset change hands at exactly the same instant. She noted, however, that this concept holds limited relevance for individual consumers, who can already transfer and settle smaller sums instantly through existing payment infrastructure such as DuitNow. Settlement remains far from instantaneous in the institutional market, though. When large sums of money are sent overseas — for purposes such as funding a child’s education — the process can take several days as funds move through traditional channels involving multiple banks. “Now, with blockchain technology, if everyone is on the same blockchain, it happens literally instantaneously,” she said. The pilot nonetheless follows a “digital twin” approach, meaning the on-chain token mirrors traditional legal records rather than replacing them entirely; the process is therefore not conducted wholly on-chain. “The technological capability [for atomic settlement] is there, but are we ready to go [completely] instantaneous? We may not be ready just yet. Imagine, it is fine if it is RM100, but it is a different story if the amount is RM100 million, for a bank. Banks are looking for less friction, but not frictionless for now,” she said. Adopting a digital twin model means banks such as CIMB are investing in testing tokenised solutions through blockchain technology, even as traditional legal records and processes continue to run in parallel — meaning cost savings have yet to materialise. However, as more processes shift on-chain in the years ahead, banking operations could become faster and more efficient, while tokenisation could also help democratise asset classes by making them more accessible to retail investors. Making Financial Markets More Efficient According to a press release, the pilot was carried out as part of CIMB’s participation in Bank Negara Malaysia’s Digital Asset Innovation Hub, which offers a controlled environment for financial institutions to test new digital asset applications. CIMB has also been engaging with the SC on the broader development of tokenised capital market products. The completion of the pilot was announced at Menara CIMB in Kuala Lumpur, at an event attended by Finance Minister II Senator Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. Amir Hamzah said the pilot demonstrates how Malaysia can build on its established strengths in Islamic finance and capital markets as financial infrastructure becomes increasingly digital. “Malaysia has developed deep capabilities in both Islamic finance and the capital markets. The next step is to ensure that these strengths continue to evolve alongside changes in technology and the way financial transactions are conducted. This pilot is important because it moves tokenisation beyond theory and tests how digital financial assets and commercial bank money can work together in a controlled environment. The objective is not digitalisation for its own sake, but to explore whether technology can make financial markets more efficient, transparent and connected while preserving strong standards of governance, investor protection and shariah compliance,” he said. Novan Amirudin, group chief executive officer of CIMB Group, said the pilot provided the bank and regulators with practical insights into the operational, legal and regulatory requirements involved in tokenised financial transactions. “This pilot allows us to test how tokenised financial assets can operate alongside existing market infrastructure and, importantly, how tokenised deposits can be used for settlement. The potential benefits are practical. Greater automation and faster settlement could reduce friction in financial transactions, improve liquidity management and increase capital efficiency. The experience gained from this pilot will help us assess how these capabilities can be developed further in Malaysia and, potentially, across regional and cross-border applications,” he said. Beyond Technology: Partnership and Integration During the press conference, Ahmad Shahriman Mohamad Shariff, CEO of Group Islamic Banking, CIMB, said an equally significant achievement of the pilot was persuading major fund management firms and government agencies to build the infrastructure required to settle CIMB’s tokenised sukuk using tokenised deposits. “If they were to choose, it is easier for them to settle [with cash] in fiat [currency], as that’s business as usual for them. But in order to join the pilot, they have to set up their own infrastructure. While we are trying to encourage people to explore [tokenisation] and onboard them, there’s a fair amount of work on their side [to be completed] as well. And we are very glad and happy to see the responses. It was well-received,” he said.

title: Banned from Sarawak – but why?
body: Kua Kia Soong In August 2007, I arrived at Kuching airport to officiate at a graduation ceremony for teachers trained by New Era College, where I was then principal. I was not carrying drugs. I was not wanted by the police. I was not entering Sarawak to organise an insurrection. I was there to attend an educational ceremony. Yet I was stopped at immigration and told that I was not allowed to enter Sarawak. After I persistently asked why, I was apparently told that I was on a blacklist because of my “anti-logging activities”. I was then put on a flight back to Kuala Lumpur. The contemporary report of the incident records that I had been an active campaigner against the Bakun Dam and had participated in a fact-finding mission concerning Indigenous people displaced from the Bakun area. Think about that for a moment. A Malaysian citizen, travelling from one part of Malaysia to another, was effectively told: you are not welcome in this part of your own country because you opposed the destruction of forests and the displacement of Indigenous communities. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Nearly 20 years later, the question remains: Sarawak may have the constitutional power to do this. But does it have the moral right? The legal argument is not the whole argument Let me be clear. I am not disputing that Sarawak possesses special immigration powers. These powers are rooted in the constitutional arrangements surrounding the formation of Malaysia. Article 161E protects certain constitutional safeguards for Sabah and Sarawak, while Part VII of the Immigration Act 1959/63 provides the statutory framework for immigration control. The Sarawak government itself describes immigration autonomy as an entrenched constitutional right. But there is a much more important question: what is that power for? The justification traditionally associated with Sarawak’s immigration safeguards was the protection of the state’s special interests – including its economy, employment, security, cultural identity and the interests of its people. The constitutional autonomy was not created as a blank cheque for excluding inconvenient Malaysians. There is a world of difference between immigration autonomy and political exclusion. If the purpose of the special powers is to protect Sarawak and Sarawakians, what exactly was Sarawak being protected from when I was turned away? A former Malaysian MP and college principal coming to officiate at a teachers’ graduation? Or an environmental campaigner who had criticised the Bakun Dam and logging? If the latter was the real reason, then the issue is no longer simply immigration administration. It becomes an issue of freedom of expression, political dissent and the abuse of administrative power. What exactly was my crime? My supposed offence was to oppose the destruction of forests and the displacement of Indigenous people. During the 1990s, I was active in opposing the Bakun Dam project. I participated in a fact-finding mission to investigate the conditions of Indigenous people displaced to Sungai Asap. So apparently, in the strange political dictionary of the time, defending forests and Indigenous communities could make a Malaysian an undesirable person in Malaysia. What next? The irony is almost unbearable. Sarawak has every reason to be proud of its unique constitutional position. But autonomy should mean more democracy, not less. It should mean that Sarawakians have greater control over their land, resources, culture and political affairs. It should not mean that the state acquires a constitutional moat around itself so that environmentalists, human rights defenders, academics or political critics can be kept outside. Otherwise, autonomy becomes a very peculiar proposition: the more autonomous the government becomes, the less accountable it becomes to citizens exercising their democratic rights. That cannot be the meaning of Malaysia’s federal bargain. Apparently, the issue has not disappeared. Just last week, Sahabat Alam Malaysia president Meenakshi Raman was denied entry into Sarawak. A Sarawak deputy minister said the state is not required to give advance notice to people barred from entering and that the relevant immigration laws give the state authority to stop people from entering. Civil society groups have called for the reasons and basis for the restriction to be disclosed. Thus, nearly two decades after my own experience, environmental defenders are still encountering the same question: Who gets to decide who is sufficiently ‘Sarawakian’ in spirit to be allowed into Sarawak? But what about international human rights? Here, the distinction between legal authority and international legitimacy becomes crucial. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights states in Article 13(2) that everyone has the right to leave any country, including his own, and to return to his country. The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights goes further in Article 12(4): “No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of the right to enter his own country.” There is, however, an important qualification: Malaysia has not ratified the covenant. Therefore, I would not argue that my exclusion in 2007 was automatically a violation of a treaty obligation binding Malaysia under the covenant. But that does not make the international human rights question disappear. The Universal Declaration remains one of the foundational statements of the international human rights system. And Malaysia has repeatedly presented itself internationally as a country committed to human rights, democracy and the rule of law. The question is therefore not merely was Sarawak legally entitled to do it? It is: was it consistent with the human rights values Malaysia claims to uphold? And that is a much harder question for the authorities to answer. Sarawak’s forests are not a Sarawak-only issue. There is another irony here. Logging, Indigenous rights, biodiversity and environmental destruction are not purely ‘state matters’ in any meaningful moral sense. The rainforest does not stop at the Kuching immigration counter. Neither does climate change. Nor does the destruction of biodiversity. Nor does the displacement of Indigenous peoples. A Malaysian citizen concerned about what happens to Sarawak’s forests is not a foreign agitator. He is a Malaysian citizen concerned about Malaysia. And if Sarawak’s forests are part of Malaysia’s natural heritage, why should Malaysians be treated as outsiders for expressing concern about them? Indeed, the more internationally connected environmental politics becomes, the more absurd such restrictions appear. Malaysia wants to attract international investment. It wants to promote Sarawak as an ecological and cultural destination. It wants to speak proudly about sustainable development and Indigenous communities. Yet an environmental campaigner can apparently arrive at an airport and be told: Turn around. Your concern for our forests is unwelcome here. What kind of message does that send to the world? A constitutional right should come with a constitutional conscience. That is a question of political morality. And it is a question that Sarawak – and Malaysia – still has to answer. Nearly 20 years after I was turned away at Kuching airport, I am still waiting for a convincing answer. – Suaram Dr Kua Kia Soong, a former MP and former director of the human rights group Suaram. title: RHB, The Makeover Guys Offer Flexi Loan for Home Purchase and Renovation
body: RHB Bank has partnered with renovation firm The Makeover Guys to offer financing that covers both a property purchase and renovation costs. The Makeover Flexi Loan provides eligible customers with financing of up to 120% of the property’s value. This comprises up to 90% for the home purchase and an additional 30% for renovation work, mortgage insurance or takaful, legal costs and documentation fees. Borrowers can repay the loan over a maximum of 35 years or until they reach the age of 70, whichever comes first. Its Full Flexi features allow them to make additional repayments and redraw funds when needed. Renovation funds will be released progressively as contractors reach project milestones. The facility is designed for homeowners and property investors. Customers can access consultation, interior design, project management and construction services through The Makeover Guys. “We have seen customers delay moving in, renovate room by room over several years or compromise on what they originally wanted because the renovation budget was not available upfront. The Makeover Flexi Loan changes that by allowing homeowners to plan both their property purchase and renovation together from day one,” said Gavin Liew, Founder & CEO of The Makeover Guys. “As homeownership needs evolve, financing solutions must evolve as well. Traditionally, property financing and renovation financing have been treated as separate decisions, even though both are fundamental to creating a home. We saw an opportunity to bridge that gap by bringing these financing needs together under a single solution,” said Sien Vee Loc, Head of Consumer Finance, Group Community Banking, RHB Bank Berhad. Featured image: (From left) Vincent Lim, Chief Revenue Officer, The Makeover Guys; Gavin Liew, Founder and Chief Executive Officer, The Makeover Guys; Sien Vee Loc, Head of Consumer Finance, RHB Bank Berhad; and Christine Wong Sze Pin, Head of Homeowners, RHB Bank Berhad.

title: FBM KLCI Edges Higher After Weak US Jobs Data
body: The FBM KLCI rebounded in early trade on Monday, supported by easing concerns over US interest rate hikes following weaker-than-expected US jobs data.  The benchmark index rose 4.53 points, or 0.28 per cent, to 1,635.39 at 9.05 am, recovering modestly after last week’s steep losses.  Banking stocks led the gains, with Maybank adding four sen to RM10.06, Hong Leong Bank rising six sen to RM22.70, Public Bank gaining four sen to RM4.70 and AMMB advancing six sen to RM6.45.  Apex Securities said it remained cautious on near-term risk appetite, noting that reduced rate hike concerns and resilient technology stocks were providing support while elevated bond yields and oil price swings could keep gains uneven.  “We remain cautious on the local bourse, as elevated bond yields and crude oil prices are likely to keep investors defensive.  “With key US labour market data pending, external headwinds should keep volatility elevated, and any recovery is likely to stay gradual until greater clarity emerges on the global rate and energy outlook,” it said in a note.  Among actively traded stocks, VS Industry rose three sen to 32 sen, Notion VTech gained 4.5 sen to 75 sen and GB Bond added 1.5 sen to 24.5 sen.

title: Nearly 9,500 buildings across Malaysia must appoint fire safety managers from April 2027, Bomba D-G says
body: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK). “From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises,” he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank here today. Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule. He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce JBPM’s workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises. “In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by JBPM for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year,” he said. Nor Hisham said to meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, JBPM expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide. He said JBPM currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony. — Bernama

title: CIMB IB says Malaysia could widen corporate tax base for Budget 2027, cut old deductions
body: CIMB IB says Malaysia could widen corporate tax base for Budget 2027, cut old deductions KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Malaysia could widen its corporate tax base by reviewing special and double deductions that have been in place for two to three decades, and remove deductions that no longer serve their original purpose, said CIMB Investment Bank. CIMB IB said, citing KPMG senior adviser on tax policy Dr Verrinderjeet Singh during a discussion, that the removal of selected deductions could lead to the government collecting more revenue while creating room for a lower headline corporate tax rate. “His [Verrinderjeet] proposal is selective: investment incentives remain important for attracting businesses, but their benefits need closer scrutiny. He links Malaysia’s shift towards outcome-based incentives to its response to Global Minimum Tax,” said CIMB IB. It added, “Their effectiveness will depend on monitoring whether investors deliver the intended economic benefits”. Malaysia’s headline corporate income tax rate is currently 24%, but the amount of tax companies ultimately pay is also affected by deductions, exemptions and investment incentives. On major tax changes, CIMB IB said Malaysia is unlikely to introduce new tax changes in Budget 2027, with stronger collection from existing taxes and a wider tax base offering the main scope for raising government revenue. The government is expected to focus on improving tax collection, particularly by bringing more businesses into the tax net and identifying income that is not fully reported. Smaller businesses are likely to offer more room for additional collections, as larger companies are already more visible to the tax authorities, said CIMB IB. “His central message was that stronger collection and targeted refinements to existing taxes offer the main near-term revenue opportunities. Against a continued focus on cost-of-living support and the social agenda, he expects few substantial tax changes in the coming budget,” said CIMB IB. E-invoicing could help identify unreported taxable activity, although smaller businesses face additional compliance and technology costs. CIMB IB said Veerinderjeet expects participation to broaden as economic conditions improve. CIMB IB also sees scope for greater use of data analytics by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) and Customs to identify businesses and income outside the existing tax net. On indirect taxes, CIMB IB said Veerinderjeet does not expect the goods and services tax (GST) to return in Budget 2027. Instead, the focus is likely to remain on improving the existing sales and service tax (SST). SST is estimated to cover about 78% to 80% of goods and services, approaching the breadth of the former GST regime. CIMB said broader exemptions for business inputs could reduce the cascading of tax costs through supply chains, although this would come at the cost of lower tax receipts. Veerinderjeet also does not expect an increase in the 2% dividend tax on annual dividend income above RM100,000, an extension of capital gains tax to listed shares or a further increase in the 30% top personal income tax rate in Budget 2027, according to the note. “Dr Veerinderjeet argues that the government should ‘sweat our assets’ through better collection, supported by greater investment in tax agency analytics. These efforts can deliver incremental gains, while broader personal, corporate and indirect tax bases offer scope to lift tax-to-GDP towards 15% over time,” said CIMB IB economists. Veerinderjeet estimates only 15% to 16% of the workforce currently pays personal income tax, with low wages limiting the number of taxpayers. Higher wages would therefore be important in expanding the personal income tax base. Budget 2027 is expected to be tabled in Parliament on Oct 9. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: Indonesia land reform raises uncertainty for Malaysian planters with exposure there — CIMB Securities
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 25): Malaysian plantation companies with sizeable operations in Indonesia face greater regulatory uncertainty following the country’s new agrarian reform law, with SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG), Genting Plantations Bhd (KL:GENP) and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KL:KLK) among those with the largest exposure, according to CIMB Securities.

The potential impact, however, remains unclear as key details — including maximum landholding limits for companies and affiliated entities, and how a provision requiring at least 20% of certain land to be made available for agrarian reform and redistribution — have yet to be finalised through implementing regulations.

As such, CIMB has not made any adjustments to its earnings forecasts or the land banks of plantation companies under its coverage, saying it sees higher regulatory uncertainty rather than an immediate loss of land or earnings.

“We do not expect an across-the-board 20% cut in existing land,” the research house said in a note on Friday.

Indonesia’s parliament approved the Agrarian Reform Law on Tuesday, creating a broader framework to address land ownership concentration, redistribution and longstanding agrarian conflicts. The law also provides for a dedicated body under the president to oversee implementation, supervision and conflict resolution.

However, the Indonesian government still needs to draw up implementing rules that will, among other matters, determine minimum and maximum landholding limits. Agrarian Affairs and Spatial Planning Minister Nusron Wahid said such details would be provided through subsequent regulations.

The development was reported earlier this week, including by Bloomberg, which highlighted broader risks to Indonesia’s plantation and property sectors. CIMB’s latest assessment focuses on the potential implications for Malaysian-listed plantation companies.

Among CIMB’s Malaysian plantation coverage, SD Guthrie, Genting Plantations and KLK have the largest absolute plantation exposure to Indonesia. IOI Corp Bhd (KL:IOICORP) has a smaller relative exposure, while Johor Plantations Group Bhd (KL:JPG), Ta Ann Holdings Bhd (KL:TAANN) and Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd (KL:HSPLANT) have plantation operations entirely in Malaysia.

CIMB said the impact will depend on the final land limits, whether the 20% rule applies to existing plantations and how it will be implemented.

Bloomberg consensus as at Friday showed analysts remaining broadly positive on SD Guthrie and Genting Plantations, while views on KLK were more mixed.

For SD Guthrie, 17 analysts had "buy" calls and three had "hold" calls, with a 12-month target price of RM7.68. Genting Plantations had 10 "buy" calls and two "hold" calls, with a target price of RM6.81. KLK had nine "buy" calls, 10 "hold" calls, and one "sell", with a target price of RM24.57.

Separately, India’s decision to lower import duties on major edible oils could provide some support for crude palm oil (CPO) demand, although CIMB expects the benefit to Malaysian planters to be modest.

India cut the basic customs duty on crude palm oil and crude soybean oil to 5% from 10%, while eliminating the 10% duty on crude sunflower oil, effective Thursday. The Indian government said the move was aimed at reducing import costs and easing domestic edible oil prices.

CIMB said the lower CPO duty should reduce landed costs and support Indian palm oil imports, although the larger tariff reduction for sunflower oil could make it more competitive against palm oil and limit the increase in demand.

India accounted for about 17% of Malaysia’s palm oil export volume in 2025. CIMB said the main benefit for Malaysian planters would likely come through firmer CPO prices rather than a significant direct increase in export volumes.

CIMB maintained its CPO price forecasts at RM4,450 per tonne for 2026 and RM4,550 per tonne for 2027.

title: Maybank completes RM2.5bil AT1 sukuk mudharabah issuance
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the issuance of RM2.5 billion additional tier 1 (AT1) sukuk mudharabah under its sukuk programme.   In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the banking group said the perpetual sukuk comprises three series with nominal amounts of RM750 million, RM1.10 billion and RM650 million, respectively.   The RM750 million tranche carries a fixed distribution rate of 4.85 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 29, 2031, while the RM1.10 billion tranche carries a rate of 5.11 per cent until its first call date on Sept 28, 2033.

title: Awards offer SMEs a benchmark for growth
body: GEORGE TOWN: Business awards can serve as more than recognition, giving small and medium enterprises (SMEs) a benchmark to measure their progress, identify areas for improvement and set targets for the year ahead, said fourth-generation entrepreneur Jonathan Chan Heng Liang. Chan, 34, the fourth-generation successor of Sin Boon Kee Coffee, said the guidelines under the Star Outstanding Business Awards (SOBA) categories provided companies with an indication of where they stood and what they could work towards next. “Joining SOBA is actually kind of one indicator for us, whether we improved since last year, what we are doing in the future and what we are aiming to hit next year. “Winning awards could also generate publicity and give customers greater confidence in a brand,” he said during SOBA Connect Penang at The Ship Campus in Batu Kawan on Sept 29. Organised by Star Media Group (SMG) and themed “Connections That Matter, Strategies That Scale”, the event attracted over 100 business owners, entrepreneurs and industry representatives for discussions on business growth, financing, technology and cybersecurity. Chan’s company, SBK Concept Store Sdn Bhd, received five recognitions at SOBA 2025, including Platinum awards for Best Employer, Best in CSR and Best in Halal Product/Service, Gold for Best Use of Technology and a Meritorious Achievement for Young Entrepreneur of the Year. He was among three speakers in the “Funding Growth: Unlocking Capital” panel, together with RHB Bank Bhd (RHB) SME Product and Programme Lending Management (PLM) development head Ian Chua and National Association of Women Entrepreneurs of Malaysia (Nawem) Penang chairman Bharati Suresh Chand. “Businesses should maintain cash reserves equivalent to three to six months of operating expenses. “This provides an important buffer to help them navigate periods of cash-flow pressure and manage their day-to-day obligations with greater confidence,” said Chua. He added that RHB views itself as a partner to SMEs, offering financing solutions tailored to their evolving business needs, whether to support short-term working capital requirements or longer-term expansion plans. “We see ourselves not just as a financier, but as a partner to SMEs. Whether businesses require short-term working capital to bridge temporary cash-flow gaps or financing to support expansion and asset acquisition, we are committed to providing solutions that meet their specific needs,” he said. The event also covered cybersecurity and data protection, an area increasingly tied to business growth. Titled “Cybersecurity & Data Protection for Business Growth”, the panel featured BitRanger Sdn Bhd chief executive officer and founder as well as Universiti Sains Malaysia Cybersecurity Research Centre (Cyres) deputy director Assoc Prof Dr Shankar Karuppayah, EY Consulting association partner Jerry Ng and Crest Asia Council chairman BK Soon and examined cybersecurity and data protection from a business perspective, as companies increasingly relied on digital systems for operations, customer engagement and growth. The programme subsequently moved to an Alumni Spotlight featuring business growth stories, with speakers sharing practical examples from their own companies. Berry Group founder and managing director Victor Tan presented his session on “Tech-Driven Growth: Turning Digital Tools into Business Advantage”, highlighting how the education group expanded from 200 students in 2020 to 10,500 in 2026. The 50-fold growth was achieved with a lean core team of 30 full-time staff while the group managed 147 tutors. He explained how the company connected six systems covering operations and culture, workforce accountability, virtual classrooms, customer engagement, enrolment automation and AI-supported teaching. Solar House business development director Ong Yong Qiang, who presented Cash Flow Mastery: Strengthening Business Stability & Growth, highlighted three factors putting pressure on business margins – the impact of the Sales and Service Tax (SST), rising material costs and changes in industry policies. He cited the July 2025 electricity tariff restructuring for medium-voltage users as an example, with lower charges per kilowatt-hour but higher charges based on maximum demand. Collaborative Excellence Sdn Bhd founder and managing partner Chong Li Ken, who presented “Future-Ready Workforce: Building Agile & Adaptive Teams”, highlighted the importance of turning individual expertise into organisational capability by capturing knowledge, processes and data, enabling businesses to build more adaptive teams and retain critical know-how as people and technology evolve. The event also saw services business pitches by the four main SOBA sponsors: Credit Guarantee Corporation Malaysia Bhd (CGC) Prai branch manager Nori Harni Juhari, U Mobile Sdn Bhd (U Mobile) head of SME Caroline Chin, RHB regional sales head SME Darren Lau and The Ship Campus chief executive officer Jasmon Lim, representing PKT Logistics Group Sdn Bhd (PKT). Lim said The Ship Campus’ role in Batu Kawan went beyond providing space for events, with the campus focused on developing an ecosystem linking businesses, education and entrepreneurship. “Our core and primary role being located in Batu Kawan was to ensure that we could build an effective ecosystem. The campus, established in 2020, engaged businesses and potential clients to understand their needs and connect them with potential suppliers, customers and other business opportunities. “The ecosystem also included Peninsula College, which offers certificates, diplomas and degrees, and Penn Skills, an accredited training centre focused on skilling, upskilling and reskilling. “Having the campus in Batu Kawan’s industrial area also placed it close to manufacturers and other companies, allowing it to understand their talent requirements and connect industry with education and skills training,” he said. SOBA 2026 is organised by SMG with CGC, PKT, RHB and U Mobile as main sponsors, while Great Wall Motor is co-sponsor, with the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) being the official trade promotion partner. It is audited by BDO while radio stations 988 and Suria are official media partners. For more information, call the SOBA Hotline at 017-231 1789or visit www.soba.com.my

title: Bursa Malaysia’s Key Index Stays Higher at Midday on Bargain Hunting
body: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 – Bursa Malaysia’s benchmark index maintained its upward momentum through the Friday morning session, rising 0.33 per cent by midday as bargain hunting in key blue-chip heavyweights supported market sentiment. At 12:30 PM, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) gained 5.44 points to reach 1,635.80, compared with Thursday’s close of 1,630.36. The index had opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87 and traded within a range of 1,630.63 to 1,640.78 throughout the morning session. Despite the rise in the benchmark index, broader market breadth remained slightly tilted toward decliners, with 507 stocks falling compared to 499 gainers. Another 494 counters traded unchanged, 1,273 remained untraded, and 24 were suspended. Half-day trading volume reached 2.24 billion shares valued at RM1.26 billion. Heavyweights and Active Counters Financial, utility, and healthcare blue chips provided the primary support to the key index: - Tenaga Nasional advanced 16 sen to RM13.06. - IHH Healthcare expanded 11 sen to RM7.81. - Maybank climbed 9 sen to RM10.04. - Public Bank added 4 sen to RM4.71. - CIMB edged down 1 sen to RM7.68. Active trading was led by technology and glove counters. JCY International surged 10 sen to 65.5 sen, Top Glove inched up 3.5 sen to 77 sen, V.S Industry ticked up 2 sen to 29 sen, and Jaks Resources added half a sen to 18.5 sen. Conversely, Zetrix AI declined 2.5 sen to 14 sen. Technology firms dominated the top gainers list: - Malaysian Pacific Industries: Surged 84 sen to RM41.96. - UWC & United Plantations: Both perked up 36 sen to RM7.46 and RM31.32, respectively. - Vitrox & UMS Integration: Both accumulated 34 sen to RM10.34 and RM8.99, respectively. Decliners were led by plantation and consumer counters: - Kuala Lumpur Kepong: Led losses, dropping 46 sen to RM20.96. - Enra: Fell 29 sen to 69 sen. - Allianz Malaysia: Declined 28 sen to RM20.72. - BLD Plantations: Shed 26 sen to RM14.74. - Dutch Lady Milk Industries: Erased 20 sen to RM29.80.
