title: Maybank Gets BNM Approval for RM4.83 Billion Ageas Deal
body: Maybank is moving ahead with its RM4.83 billion Ageas deal after securing Bank Negara Malaysia’s approval. The bank signed an unconditional agreement on 8 September to acquire Ageas Insurance International’s remaining 30.95% stake in Maybank Ageas Holdings. Maybank will carry out the acquisition through its wholly owned subsidiary Etiqa International Holdings, which currently owns 69.05% of the company. The deal will give the bank full control of Etiqa’s insurance and takaful businesses in Malaysia and Singapore. BNM granted the required approvals on 1 September. The Monetary Authority of Singapore had approved the transaction in March. Maybank will fund the purchase entirely through internally generated funds. It will also pay Ageas a RM34.17 million fee accrued from 1 August until the targeted completion date. Maybank Ageas Holdings will distribute a RM799.99 million dividend to its existing shareholders upon completion. Etiqa International Holdings will receive RM552.38 million, while Ageas will receive RM247.61 million. The bank expects the acquisition to support its regional expansion and allow closer integration between its banking and insurance services. The deal does not require approval from Maybank shareholders and is expected to be completed on 11 September 2026. title: Bursa Malaysia Index Falls Amid Heavyweight Declines
body: Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia continued to experience a downturn at mid-morning, largely driven by selling pressures in leading sectors such as healthcare, industrial products, and utilities. According to BERNAMA News Agency, at 11 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped by 11.73 points to 1,639.44, compared to the previous day's close of 1,651.17, after opening slightly lower at 1,649.87. In the healthcare sector, IHH Healthcare saw a decrease of 13 sen to RM7.70. Within industrial products, Petronas Chemicals fell 11 sen to RM4.07, Press Metal Aluminium went down nine sen to RM7.36, and Sunway dipped two sen to RM4.40. Utilities counters also took a hit, with YTL Power dropping six sen to RM5.81, YTL Corporation declining by one sen to RM2.27, and Tenaga Nasional decreasing by two sen to RM12.94. The overall market saw 484 decliners surpassing 273 gainers, with 460 counters unchanged. Additionally, 1,556 counters remained untraded, and 12 were suspended. The market turnover was recorded at 1.18 billion shares valued at RM769.76 million. Hong Leong Investment Bank noted that the ongoing US-Iran tensions and the Federal Reserve's hawkish stance could prolong the benchmark index's risk-off consolidation, influenced by high oil prices, bond yields, and continued foreign outflows. Among major stocks, Maybank and CIMB each dropped by two sen to RM9.97 and RM7.77, respectively, while Public Bank declined three sen to RM4.67. In active trades, Zetrix AI increased by half a sen to 16.5 sen, V.S Industry rose one sen to 29 sen, Jaks Resources fell half a sen to 20 sen, ACE Market newcomer GB Bond decreased by 2.5 sen to 22.5 sen, and Dagang Nexchange rose two sen to 50.5 sen. Top gainers included Malaysian Pacific Industries, which increased by 62 sen to RM41.02, Malayan Cement rising by 12 sen to RM5.57, and both MI Technovation and Hengyuan Refining gaining 10 sen to RM5.30 and RM3.66, respectively. Vitrox saw an increase of eight sen to RM9.99. Conversely, Kuala Lumpur Kepong led the decliners, falling 74 sen to RM21.46, followed by Allianz Malaysia, which shed 68 sen to RM20.94. Nestle fell 40 sen to RM89.60, United Plantations dropped 30 sen to RM31.26, and Hong Leong Bank lost 28 sen to RM22.86. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index decreased by 71.17 points to 17,503.50, the FBM Emas Index fell 72.18 points to 12,219.83, and the FBM Top 100 Index declined by 76.32 points to 12,008.12. The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened by 71.61 points to 12,104.73, and the FBM ACE Index decreased by 22.64 points to 5,511.64. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index dropped by 1.24 points to 179.17, the Energy Index eased by 5.43 points to 840.27, the Financial Services Index fell 87.09 points to 19,129.40, and the Plantation Index retreated by 104.26 points to 9,092.41.

title: FBM KLCI Rebounds Slightly on Fed Pause Hopes
body: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The FBM KLCI opened higher on Monday, rising 4.53 points to 1,635.39 at 9.05am, supported by weaker U.S. jobs data that eased inflation concerns and strengthened expectations of a Federal Reserve rate pause. FBM KLCI Rebounds Banking stocks led gains, with Maybank up four sen to RM10.06, Hong Leong Bank adding six sen to RM22.70, Public Bank climbing four sen to RM4.70 and AMMB rising six sen to RM6.45. Among actively traded counters, VS Industry gained three sen to 32 sen, Notion VTech rose 4.5 sen to 75 sen, and GB Bond added 1.5 sen to 24.5 sen. Analysts remain cautious, citing elevated bond yields and oil price swings as factors likely to keep investors defensive and gains uneven in the near term. #businessnews FBM KLCI, Malaysian banks, Fed pause hopes, market volatility Table of Contents Read More News on Latest Malaysia Follow us on: Read More News on Business News Malaysia Read More News on SG Business News Read More News on World Future TV

title: Jamin peruntukan awam universiti, hentikan korporatisasi UiTM – Suara Siswa UiTM
body: Suara Siswa UiTM menggesa Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi (KPT) dan Kementerian Kewangan menjamin peruntukan awam yang mencukupi dan berterusan kepada universiti awam, susulan perkembangan terbaharu berkaitan UiTM Holdings yang, menurut kumpulan itu, mencerminkan masalah lebih besar dalam model pembiayaan pendidikan tinggi. Kumpulan mahasiswa itu berkata pengakuan Menteri Pendidikan Tinggi Zambry Kadir pada 27 September bahawa kerajaan tidak lagi menanggung sepenuhnya keperluan kewangan universiti sejak 2017 menunjukkan universiti awam semakin didorong mencari sumber pendapatan sendiri, termasuk melalui syarikat pegangan, pelaburan dan kegiatan komersial. KPT pada masa sama mengakui sebahagian syarikat pegangan universiti tidak berfungsi dengan baik, dan proses meneliti serta menyusun semula syarikat berkenaan telah dimulakan sejak tahun lalu. Menurut Suara Siswa UiTM, UiTM Holdings tidak wajar dilihat semata-mata sebagai sebuah syarikat yang mengalami masalah kewangan. KPT sebelum ini mengesahkan kerugian sebelum cukai terkumpul UiTM Holdings sekitar RM157j bagi 2017, 2018, 2019 dan 2021, manakala Jawatankuasa Kira-Kira Wang Negara (PAC) pernah merekodkan suntikan modal UiTM berjumlah RM260j juta kepada syarikat itu antara 2007 hingga 2018 serta membangkitkan isu pematuhan dan tadbir urus. Kumpulan itu berkata perkembangan berkenaan perlu dibaca bersama dasar kewangan pendidikan tinggi negara. Menurut Pelan Pembangunan Pendidikan Tinggi Malaysia 2015-25 (PPPM) merekodkan sumbangan kerajaan kepada universiti awam bukan universiti penyelidikan turun daripada 85% perbelanjaan operasi pada 2015 kepada 76% pada 2022, sementara pendapatan dijana sendiri meningkat daripada 21% kepada 22%. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Dokumen itu mengenal pasti kemampanan kewangan sebagai cabaran utama institut pengajian tinggi. Suara Siswa UiTM berkata keadaan itu menunjukkan universiti awam semakin diletakkan di bawah tekanan untuk mencapai kelestarian kewangan melalui penjanaan pendapatan, termasuk pelaburan, kegiatan komersial, konsultansi dan model perniagaan baharu. PPPM secara jelas meletakkan penjanaan pendapatan, pendanaan berasaskan prestasi dan model perniagaan inovatif sebagai sebahagian daripada agenda kelestarian kewangan institusi. [Hala tuju ini diteruskan dan diperkukuh dalam Rancangan Pendidikan Tinggi Malaysia 2026-35.] “Kami melihat persoalan UiTM Holdings sebagai sebahagian daripada masalah korporatisasi pendidikan tinggi,” kata kumpulan itu. “Apabila pembiayaan awam dikurangkan, risiko kewangan tidak hilang, tetapi dipindahkan kepada universiti untuk ditanggung melalui pasaran dan akhirnya kepada mahasiswa melalui pelbagai bentuk kos pendidikan dan sara hidup.” Suara Siswa UiTM menggesa kerajaan mengembalikan pembiayaan awam sebagai asas utama kewangan universiti, dengan peruntukan KPT dan Kementerian Kewangan yang mencukupi untuk menanggung fungsi teras seperti pengajaran, penyelidikan, penyelenggaraan kampus dan kebajikan mahasiswa tanpa memaksa universiti bergantung kepada keuntungan aktiviti komersial. Kumpulan itu turut menyeru supaya yuran dan kos wajib pendidikan dikurangkan secara berperingkat sehingga pendidikan tinggi awam dapat dinyahkomodifikasikan. Kumpulan mahasiswa itu turut menuntut supaya sebarang penyusunan semula UiTM Holdings tidak berakhir dengan sekadar mencari model perniagaan baharu atau menutup kerugian melalui suntikan dana awam tanpa perubahan struktur. Ia mahu kerajaan menilai semula aktiviti komersial universiti berdasarkan kepentingan pendidikan dan masyarakat, di samping memastikan pekerja universiti tidak menjadi pihak yang menanggung kesan penstrukturan. Dalam perkembangan berasingan, Suruhanjaya Pencegah Rasuah Malaysia mengesahkan siasatan terhadap UiTM Holdings masih berjalan dan melibatkan isu teknikal serta kelemahan tadbir urus, termasuk dakwaan pembayaran RM42j berkaitan projek solar 50MW di Gambang, yang dikatakan dibuat tanpa kelulusan lembaga pengarah dan bagi tujuan yang tidak berkaitan dengan projek. Suara Siswa UiTM berkata sebarang pertuduhan jenayah hendaklah tertakluk kepada hasil siasatan dan proses undang-undang, namun isu tadbir urus dan model pembiayaan universiti boleh dipersoalkan secara berasingan. “Universiti awam tidak sepatutnya dipaksa menjadi perusahaan yang mencari keuntungan untuk membiayai fungsi awamnya,” kata kumpulan itu. “Peruntukan pendidikan ialah tanggungjawab negara, manakala kekayaan dan aset universiti harus diprioritikan untuk mahasiswa, pekerja, pengajaran, penyelidikan dan kepentingan masyarakat.” – Suara Siswa UiTM The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. title: Bar Fails in Bid to Challenge Ex-AG Terrirudin's Appointment to Judicial Appointments Commission
body: "The JAC merely recommends. The power of appointment lies with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the prime minister’s advice under [the law]. The alleged fear of bias from one of nine members of a body that decides nothing is remote, indirect, and speculative.” — High Court judge Norliza Othman. KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The Malaysian Bar has failed to get the green light to challenge former attorney general (AG) and sitting Federal Court judge Tan Sri Ahmad Terrirudin Mohd Salleh's appointment to the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC). In dismissing the Bar's leave (permission) application to commence a judicial review, High Court judge Norliza Othman on Monday said that Terrirudin's appointment satisfies the criterium in law, namely that an apex court judge must be appointed by the prime minister. She said that the law does not extend to other implied requirements, such as seniority or length of service, as contended by the Bar. "[The law] is plain. It specifies the category of person: a Federal Court judge; and the appointing authority: the prime minister — and stops there. The applicant asserts both are satisfied, yet asks the court to read in implied requirements: seniority, length of service, prior High Court/Court of Appeal experience, freedom from unresolved allegations, consultation, and conformity with an asserted convention — none of which appear in the text. "Our function is to interpret the words used, not to supply the words omitted," she said adding that case law is against the Bar in this case. Terrirudin, who was appointed a Federal Court judge in November 2025, is serving a two-year term on the JAC, from Nov 15, 2025 to Nov 14, 2027. The JAC is a nine-member body responsible for recommending candidates for appointment to Malaysia's superior courts. The ex-AG's appointment drew brickbats from many quarters, with many highlighting that his selection departed from established practice by bypassing a more senior judge and could undermine perceptions of judicial independence. In the midst of this, the Bar filed the leave application on Feb 12, naming Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, the JAC, and the Malaysian government as respondents. Among the reliefs sought, the Bar is asking the court to quash Terrirudin's appointment, prohibit his appointment to any judicial office pending disposal of the proceedings, and compel the disclosure of minutes from a JAC meeting held on May 16, 2025. In her grounds of judgement, Norliza said that the Bar's argument that Terriruddin's appointment was irrational fails, as "nothing here is so deprived of logic or accepted moral standards that no sensible decision-maker could have reached it". She added that the Bar's argument that the decision contained illegality also failed. She added that the Bar also lacked locus standi to bring the action as they were not adversely affected by the appointment. "The JAC merely recommends," she said in her judgement, adding, "The power of appointment lies with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the prime minister's advice under [the law]. The alleged fear of bias from one of nine members of a body that decides nothing is remote, indirect, and speculative.” She ordered cost of RM3,000 to be paid to the Attorney General's Chambers (AGC). Former Bar presidents Zainur Zakaria, Steven Thiru and Datuk Ambiga Sreevenasan appeared for the Bar while senior federal counsel Datuk Shamsul Bolhassan led the team appearing for the AGC. title: Budget 2027 could deliver double relief for businesses, middle-income Malaysians - CIMB securities | Business | The Vibes
body: MALAYSIAN businesses and middle-income households could receive a double boost from Budget 2027 through wider sales and service tax (SST) exemptions and targeted personal income tax cuts, potentially easing operating and living costs, CIMB Securities says. CIMB Securities, in a research note, said there was scope to broaden SST exemptions for production-related inputs as businesses continued to face elevated energy, logistics and other operating costs. It expects further SST relief to reduce government collections by about RM1 billion, although underlying economic growth should still lift SST revenue by 5.5% to RM72 billion in 2027. Unlike the goods and services tax (GST), SST does not have a general input tax credit mechanism, meaning businesses can pay tax on inputs without being able to deduct it against tax charged on their own sales. This can result in tax costs being embedded throughout the supply chain, CIMB said. The research house expects extending selected exemptions to be the more immediate option in Budget 2027, while a broader input tax credit mechanism could be introduced from 2028 or later because of the additional administrative and refund framework required. For households, CIMB sees scope for targeted personal income tax relief for middle-income taxpayers, particularly those facing higher living costs but receiving less direct cash assistance. As an illustration, it said tax rates for chargeable income of RM50,001 to RM70,000 and RM70,001 to RM100,000 could each be reduced by one percentage point to 10% and 18%, respectively. The current 25% tax bracket could also be split, with a 24% rate applied to chargeable income between RM100,001 and RM150,000. Such a package could provide annual tax savings of RM200 for taxpayers with RM70,000 in chargeable income, RM500 at RM100,000 and up to RM1,000 for those with RM150,000 and above, CIMB estimated. It said the illustrative tax package would cost the government about RM800 million a year. More broadly, CIMB expects Budget 2027 to continue providing household support while maintaining fiscal consolidation, forecasting the fiscal deficit to narrow slightly to 3.4% of gross domestic product in 2027 from an estimated 3.5% in 2026. The research house also expects cash assistance under Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah to increase by RM2 billion to RM17 billion, supported partly by lower fuel subsidy spending. CIMB forecasts petrol and diesel subsidies to fall to RM32 billion in 2027 from RM41 billion, creating room for higher household assistance and development spending while keeping the government on its fiscal consolidation path. Budget 2027, the fifth Madani Budget and the second under the 13th Malaysia Plan, is scheduled to be tabled in Parliament on Oct 9. The Ministry of Finance has said the budget will focus on areas including cost-of-living pressures, business competitiveness and productivity while maintaining fiscal discipline.

title: World Bank Supports Malaysia’s Possible Integration of GST Elements Into SST
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): The World Bank has agreed that certain elements of the goods and services tax (GST) should be implemented into Malaysia’s sales and service tax (SST) to address its distortionary features. World Bank lead economist for Malaysia Apurva Sanghi said the government should address the SST’s nature as a cascading tax and, in turn, an embedded tax. The SST is a single-stage tax with no input credit mechanism. In other words, tax can become embedded in prices as goods and services move through the supply chain. “We believe what is required is neutral tax reform that relieves cascading and embedded effects on businesses, for example through input tax credits, while also broadening the tax base to bolster revenues," he said during a briefing on the October 2026 Malaysia Economic Monitor report. There has been much industry and policy discussion on what an integration of GST elements into the SST, or a formulation of a better SST, could look like. Discourse began after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the government is studying improvements to the existing SST, including whether it can incorporate elements of the GST, following a Budget 2027 engagement session in August. Malaysia implemented the GST in 2015 at a 6% rate under the administration of Datuk Seri Najib Razak. The implementation led to soaring inflation and widespread complaints of slow tax refunds that created a cash crunch for small- to medium-sized businesses. The tax was suspended on June 1, 2018, after Pakatan Harapan took over the federal government, and was subsequently abolished and replaced with the current SST on Sept 1, 2018. While Apurva agreed the SST can be improved if the cascading tax aspect is addressed, he did note the World Bank has held the view that the GST is a better solution, should its regressivity be offset with cash transfers to those vulnerable. “Trying to integrate GST elements with SST, I think of it as trying to integrate efficiency with empathy. “And, when you fuse both together, the risk is you may get neither,” he warned. GST, all being equal, is favourable to SST, Apurva noted. He said GST avoids cascading and embedded tax. “One of the stumbling blocks of GST 1.0, the previous GST regime, was the delay in issuing refunds. If that is addressed, then that definitely is yet another argument to think about GST,” he said. World Bank economist Deisigan Shammugam also highlighted that it has been a decade since then and that technology has improved since then. title: 银行股突遭抛售潮 马股重摔至今年新低！
body: 银行股突遭抛售潮 马股重摔至今年新低！ （吉隆坡7日讯）银行股再次遭到抛售，拖累马股今早开市不久便面临沉重卖压，早盘一度暴跌超过18点或1.1%，不仅失守1630点关卡，还创下今年来新低。 富马隆综指今早以1633.54点迎市，随着银行股陷入沉重卖压，早盘一度重挫18.54点至1614.81点，写下今年来新低，同时也是去年12月以来最低。 截至早上11时，隆综指跌16.16点或0.99%至1617.19点，成交量有5亿4777万2000股。 银行股今日齐聚下跌股榜，当中以联昌集团（CIMB，1023，主要板金服）卖压最重，早盘以7.7令吉迎市后不断探低，盘中低见7.35令吉，跌35仙或4.5%。 该股目前报7.37令吉，挫33仙或4.3%，成交量有1211万6600股，为全场第3大下跌股。 大盘料维持盘整 大马银行集团（AMBANK，1015，主要板金服）一度大跌4.2%至6.20令吉，丰隆银行（HLBANK，5819，主要板金服）则跌2.2%至21.60令吉。 马银行（MAYBANK，1155，主要板金服）早盘虽曾回升至10令吉，在仍不敌抛售潮，最新跌7仙至9.90令吉，暂有605万9200股易手。 丰隆投行研究指出，政府将在本周五（9日）提呈2027年财政预算案，而美国与伊朗紧张局势升温，加上美联储持续释放鹰派讯号，预计将令隆综指维持避险情绪下的盘整走势。 此外，在油价高企、债券收益率攀升，以及外资持续撤出的背景下，市场风险偏好料受压。 数据显示，截至周二（6日），外资净卖600万令吉的马股，已连续10个交易日从马股撤资；10月迄今累计净卖3亿4100万令吉，今年来净卖出达64亿9000万令吉。 散户在周二同样净卖4500万令吉，反观本地机构已连续五个交易日进场扶盘，昨日净买5100万令吉的马股。 The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: The Makeover Guys and RHB Bank Introduce the Makeover Flexi Loan with Up to 120% Financing for Home Purchase and Renovation
body: KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA – Media OutReach Newswire – 15 September 2026 – The Makeover Guys has partnered with RHB Bank Berhad as RHB Bank’s Home Makeover Partner to introduce the Makeover Flexi Loan– an integrated financing solution that enables eligible customers to finance both their home purchase and renovation under a single facility, with financing support of up to 120% of the property’s value. Demand for home renovations continues to rise in Malaysia. The home improvement and renovation market was valued at RM47.7 billion in 2024 and is projected to grow to RM59.2 billion by 2029, as more homeowners invest in upgrading their living spaces to suit changing lifestyles and personal preferences. While home financing is widely available, renovation financing is often treated as a separate borrowing decision. This means many homeowners need to secure additional financing or rely on personal savings after purchasing a property before they can begin renovations. The Makeover Flexi Loan, Powered by RHB Bank offers a different approach by enabling eligible customers to finance both their home purchase and renovation under a single facility. Instead of managing separate financing arrangements, homeowners can plan both from the outset, providing greater financial certainty and a more seamless homeownership journey. The Makeover Flexi Loan, Powered by RHB Bank offers: - Up to 120% financing under a single facility for home purchase and renovation - Up to 90% financing for the property purchase, with an additional up to 30% for renovation works, Mortgage Reducing Term Assurance or Takaful (MRTA/MRTT), and legal and documentation fees - Financing tenure of up to 35 years, or until the borrower reaches the age of 70, whichever comes first - Full Flexi features, allowing customers to make additional repayments and redraw funds based on their financial needs - Progressive disbursement of renovation financing according to contractor milestones throughout the renovation process and is suitable for both homeowners and property investors “Every month, we meet homeowners who are excited to receive the keys to their new homes, only to realise that renovation requires another significant financial commitment. A typical renovation can cost anywhere between RM50,000 and RM150,000, depending on the property type, and many buyers simply are not prepared for that additional expense immediately after purchasing their home,” said Gavin Liew, Founder & CEO of The Makeover Guys We have seen customers delay moving in, renovate room by room over several years or compromise on what they originally wanted because the renovation budget was not available upfront. The Makeover Flexi Loan changes that by allowing homeowners to plan both their property purchase and renovation together from day one. It gives them greater financial certainty and makes it easier to create a home that reflects the way they want to live,” Gavin added. “As homeownership needs evolve, financing solutions must evolve as well. Traditionally, property financing and renovation financing have been treated as separate decisions, even though both are fundamental to creating a home. We saw an opportunity to bridge that gap by bringing these financing needs together under a single solution,” said Sien Vee Loc, Head of Consumer Finance, Group Community Banking, RHB Bank Berhad. Partnering with The Makeover Guys allows us to combine RHB’s financing expertise with trusted renovation capabilities to address a growing market need. Together, we are making it easier for eligible customers to move from purchasing a property to creating a home that meets their lifestyle and investment goals,” Vee Loc added. As Malaysia’s housing market continues to evolve and more buyers enter the market, expectations are shifting beyond financing the purchase of a property to supporting the homeownership journey as a whole. The residential segment remained the largest contributor to Malaysia’s property market in the first quarter of 2026, accounting for 58.8% of all property transactions, with nearly 53,000 residential transactions worth more than RM22 billion. The collaboration connects customers with The Makeover Guys’ end-to-end renovation expertise, providing a complete renovation experience spanning consultation, curated interior design, project management and construction, allowing customers to move from financing their property to completing their home through a single, connected journey.Rather than managing financing, renovation and project delivery separately, customers can now plan every stage together, providing greater certainty over costs, timelines and the overall renovation experience. The partnership further strengthens its commitment to making quality renovations more accessible by combining trusted renovation expertise with financing solutions that support customers from the moment they purchase a property through to the completion of their home. Through this collaboration, The Makeover Guys and RHB Bank are bringing financing and renovation closer together, giving homeowners and property investors a more connected way to plan, finance and complete one of life’s most important investments. For more information regarding the Makeover Flexi Loan, Powered by RHB Bank, kindly visit https://www.themakeover.my/contact to drop your enquiry. title: DNB selesai pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion, pacu fasa baharu pertumbuhan 5G Malaysia
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) berjaya menyelesaikan pembiayaan berjangka Islamik bersindiket bernilai RM5.2 bilion, sekali gus mengukuhkan kedudukan kewangan syarikat bagi menyokong perkembangan rangkaian 5G Malaysia.  Transaksi berkenaan antara kemudahan pinjaman bersindiket terbesar pernah diatur untuk sebuah syarikat tidak tersenarai di Malaysia.  Maybank Investment Bank Berhad bertindak sebagai Mandated Lead Arranger, Bookrunner dan Coordinating Arranger, manakala AmInvestment Bank Berhad, CIMB Islamic Bank Berhad, RHB Islamic Bank Berhad dan United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Berhad bertindak sebagai Joint Mandated Lead Arrangers.  AmInvestment Bank Berhad pula bertindak sebagai penasihat kewangan kepada DNB.  Menurut DNB, kejayaan menyelesaikan pembiayaan itu merupakan perkembangan penting dalam evolusi syarikat ketika Malaysia memasuki fasa seterusnya dalam pelaksanaan rangkaian 5G dwi-rangkaian.  Pembiayaan berkenaan dijangka mengukuhkan kedudukan kewangan jangka panjang DNB selain memudah cara perancangan keluar MOF Inc. sebagai pemegang saham biasa syarikat.  Ia seterusnya membuka laluan kepada struktur pemilikan sama rata antara pemegang saham syarikat telekomunikasi mudah alih (MNO), iaitu CelcomDigi Berhad menerusi Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd dan YTL Power International Bhd.  Peralihan kepada struktur pemilikan tersebut dijangka berlaku pada awal suku keempat 2026.  Bagaimanapun, MOF Inc. akan mengekalkan satu saham khas dalam DNB bagi melindungi kepentingan nasional.  Menurut DNB, saham khas itu akan membolehkan kerajaan terus memainkan peranan dalam perkara strategik utama, pada masa sama memberi ruang kepada syarikat meneruskan fasa pembangunan seterusnya.  Pembiayaan bersindiket itu turut merangkumi pembiayaan semula Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF) DNB yang tamat tempoh pada 29 September 2026.  Langkah itu turut mewujudkan struktur pembiayaan jangka panjang yang lebih mampan bagi menyokong pertumbuhan DNB pada masa depan.  Spektrum 240 MHz diperkukuh  Penyelesaian pembiayaan itu turut dibuat serentak dengan pemberian penuh spektrum 100 MHz dalam jalur 3.3 hingga 3.4 GHz atau F0 serta penukaran keseluruhan pegangan spektrum DNB berjumlah 240 MHz kepada Spectrum Assignment.  DNB berkata, selepas Spectrum Assignment dikeluarkan Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (MCMC), penugasan itu berkuat kuasa mulai 1 Oktober 2026.  Perkembangan itu memberikan kepastian kawal selia yang lebih tinggi selain mengukuhkan keupayaan DNB untuk menyokong keperluan kesalinghubungan 5G Malaysia yang semakin berkembang.  Pegangan spektrum 240 MHz berkenaan dijangka meningkatkan kapasiti, kecekapan dan prestasi rangkaian, sekali gus membolehkan kelajuan lebih tinggi, kependaman lebih rendah serta pengalaman pelanggan yang lebih baik.  Ia turut menyokong penggunaan teknologi 5G yang lebih maju termasuk Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced serta keupayaan rangkaian berasaskan kecerdasan buatan (AI).  DNB berkata, gabungan pembiayaan baharu dan penugasan spektrum itu akan memperkukuh keupayaan syarikat meningkatkan kualiti serta daya tahan rangkaian, memenuhi permintaan masa depan dan menyokong aspirasi ekonomi digital Malaysia.  Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif DNB, Datuk Azman Ismail, berkata penyelesaian pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion itu merupakan pencapaian penting yang mencerminkan keyakinan terhadap asas perniagaan, rekod operasi serta peranan jangka panjang syarikat dalam ekonomi digital Malaysia.  “Pembiayaan ini menyediakan platform yang mampan untuk DNB beroperasi secara sendiri, meneruskan pelaburan dalam peningkatan rangkaian dan peluasan kapasiti serta memanfaatkan aset spektrum kami yang telah diperluaskan.  “Ketika Malaysia bergerak maju di bawah rangkaian dwi-rangkaian, DNB kekal komited menyediakan infrastruktur digital bertaraf dunia yang menyokong pemegang saham, pelanggan, perusahaan dan agensi kerajaan,” katanya.  Beliau berkata, dengan kedudukan kewangan yang kukuh, sumber spektrum yang dipertingkatkan serta platform 5G nasional yang telah terbukti, DNB berada pada kedudukan untuk menyokong aspirasi kerajaan menjadikan Malaysia sebagai negara berteraskan AI.  “DNB akan membantu memacu fasa seterusnya pertumbuhan digital Malaysia,” katanya.  DNB turut merakamkan penghargaan kepada pemegang sahamnya, CelcomDigi, Maxis dan YTL, atas keyakinan serta sokongan berterusan terhadap syarikat.  Penghargaan turut diberikan kepada Kerajaan Malaysia dan MCMC atas bimbingan serta sokongan dalam menjayakan agenda transformasi digital negara.  DNB turut mengucapkan terima kasih kepada institusi kewangan dan penasihat, penasihat undang-undang serta penyedia perkhidmatan lain yang menyumbang kepakaran bagi memastikan transaksi pembiayaan itu berjaya diselesaikan.

title: Why is Malaysia sending back Rohingya refugees to Myanmar?
body: They sought refuge in Malaysia nearly a decade ago, fleeing persecution and war in Myanmar. But thousands of Rohingya refugees are being sent back to a nation still plagued by violence. The Malaysian government is facing accusations of forcibly deporting the refugees – a charge the goverment denies. It says the process is voluntary and coordinated with Myanmar’s government. But human rights groups say this process violates international law by sending refugees to countries where they risk facing prosecution or torture. So, will this concern stop the Rohingya being sent back to Myanmar? title: Aktiviti buru saham pacu Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi, sentimen positif
body: Bursa Malaysia meningkat selepas mengalami pemulihan kecil pada akhir dagangan Jumaat, dipacu oleh aktiviti memburu saham-saham berharga rendah susulan jualan ketara baru-baru ini, kata penganalisis.  Lantunan itu bagaimanapun kekurangan momentum ketika pasaran Asia kekal diasak tekanan menjelang pengumuman data pasaran tenaga kerja Amerika Syarikat (AS).  Pada 5 petang, indeks penunjuk utama FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) menokok 0.51 mata atau 0.03 peratus kepada 1,630.87 daripada paras penutup 1,630.36, semalam.  Indeks penanda aras itu yang dibuka menokok 3.51 mata kepada 1,633.87, bergerak dalam jajaran 1,630.63 hingga 1,640.78 sepanjang sesi dagangan.  Sentimen pasaran positif dengan kaunter untung mengatasi rugi iaitu 585 berbanding 541 manakala 558 lain tidak berubah, 1,089 tidak diniagakan dan 24 lain digantung dagangannya.  Jumlah dagangan meningkat kepada 4.23 bilion unit bernilai RM2.70 bilion daripada 3.1 bilion unit bernilai RM2.7 bilion, semalam.  Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata aktiviti penjualan pada baru-baru ini menyaksikan penilaian saham mewah yang lebih menarik, sekali gus berpotensi menggalakkan usaha pengumpulan saham secara berperingkat.  Namun pada masa sama, katanya, pelabur terus mengambil langkah untuk kekal bertahan berikutan perkembangan seperti hasil bon dan harga minyak mentah yang kekal tinggi.  “Bagi bursa tempatan pula, kami berpendirian berhati-hati di disebalik peningkatan berikutan risiko cabaran luar yang mungkin mengekalkan ketidaktentuan pasaran pada tahap tinggi,” katanya kepada Bernama.  Saham wajaran tinggi menyaksikan Maybank naik tujuh sen kepada RM10.02, Public Bank susut satu sen kepada RM4.66, CIMB berkurangan empat sen kepada RM7.65, Tenaga Nasional meningkat enam sen kepada RM12.96 dan IHH Healthcare meraih 10 sen kepada RM7.80.  Saham paling aktif menyaksikan Zetrix AI susut lima sen kepada 11.5 sen, Jaks Resources tidak berubah pada 18 sen, JCY International menokok 10.5 sen kepada 66 sen, V.S Industry naik dua sen kepada 29 sen dan PUC menambah satu sen kepada 4.5 sen.  Bagi saham paling untung, Malaysian Pacific Industries melonjak RM1.28 kepada RM42.40, UWC naik 47 sen kepada RM7.57, Vitrox menokok 46 sen kepada RM10.46, United Plantations meraih 42 sen kepada RM31.38 manakala UMS Integration meningkat 38 sen kepada RM9.03.  Saham yang mencatatkan penurunan ketara diterajui oleh Nestle yang susut 48 sen kepada RM89.52, Kuala Lumpur Kepong turun 42 sen kepada RM21, Enra berkurangan 25.5 sen kepada 72.5 sen manakala Allianz Malaysia dan Hong Leong Bank masing-masing menguncup 20 sen kepada RM20.80 dan RM22.64.  Di papan indeks pula, Indeks FBM Mid 70 meningkat 122.94 mata kepada 17,481.93, Indeks FBM Emas menokok 27.04 mata kepada 12,170.57 manakala Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 24.52 mata kepada 11,957.68.  Indeks FBM Emas Syariah meningkat 47.31 mata kepada 12,060.32 manakala Indeks FBM ACE menokok 46.49 mata kepada 5,529.46.  Prestasi sektor menyaksikan Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian naik 0.79 mata kepada 178.52, Indeks Tenaga susut 1.98 mata kepada 833.03, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan menguncup 20.40 mata kepada 19,040.51 manakala Indeks Perladangan meningkat 29.97 mata kepada 9,056.55.  Jumlah dagangan di Pasaran Utama meningkat kepada 2.67 bilion unit bernilai RM2.34 bilion daripada 1.82 bilion unit bernilai RM2.42 bilion, semalam.  Waran melonjak kepada 973.40 juta unit bernilai RM160.21 juta daripada 618.78 juta unit bernilai RM72.71 juta sebelum ini.  Di Pasaran ACE, jumlah dagangan susut kepada 593.05 juta unit bernilai RM205.21 juta daripada 650.13 juta unit bernilai RM226.92 juta sebelumnya.  Kaunter produk pengguna dan perkhidmatan menyumbang sebanyak 241.01 juta saham yang diniagakan di Pasaran Utama manakala produk dan perkhidmatan perindustrian (266.57 juta), pembinaan (183.37 juta), teknologi (1.41 bilion), perkhidmatan kewangan (50.26 juta), hartanah (152.37 juta), perladangan (19.73 juta), amanah pelaburan hartanah (15.78 juta), dana tertutup (214,200), tenaga (99.69 juta), penjagaan kesihatan (103.06 juta) telekomunikasi dan media (28.89 juta), pengangkutan dan logistik (47.35 juta), utiliti (46.61 juta) dan amanah perniagaan (119,600) .

title: Rapidus Taps Four Malaysian Firms as Design Solution Associates for CORE Ecosystem
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Rapidus Corporation has roped in Malaysian firms — GreatAsic Technology Sdn Bhd, Infinecs Systems Sdn Bhd, Oppstar Bhd's (KL:OPPSTAR) Oppstar Technology Sdn Bhd and SkyeChip Bhd (KL:SKYECHIP) — as design solution associates to support the development of its global chip ecosystem framework. The Japan-backed Rapidus said it will establish the Rapidus Collaborative Open Rapid Ecosystem (CORE), a global ecosystem framework to support the development and mass production of cutting-edge semiconductors. As the first Rapidus CORE initiative, Rapidus said it is forming a group of design solution associates, which include 17 firms. "Today, semiconductor development requires more than just manufacturing technology; it is essential to integrate the entire semiconductor value chain — including research institutions, EDA (Electronic Design Automation), IP (intellectual property), design and manufacturing — to provide customers with a development and production infrastructure they can rely on. "Further, amid a global shortage of cutting-edge semiconductor talent, it is crucial to build a design ecosystem that enables customers to begin development at an early stage by collaborating with design-related companies," Rapidus said in a statement on Monday. The 17 firms include Malaysian companies, namely GreatAsic Technology, Infinecs Systems, Oppstar Technology, and SkyeChip. Other firms include Japan's Dai Nippon Printing, TOPPAN Inc, Toshiba Information Systems, MavissDesign, and NSW Inc and London-based AION Silicon. Also listed were Indian firms namely HCL Technologies Ltd, Infosys Ltd, Moschip Technologies ltd, and Wipro Ltd; US-based companies Cadence Design Systems and Synopsys, as well as Singapore's Quest Global Services. Design solution associates will serve as a bridge between customers and Rapidus, providing each company's design resources and specialised expertise to support the rapid evolution of semiconductor development. This will enable Rapidus to strengthen its support system — from design through manufacturing — to meet customer needs both in Japan and overseas. Moving forward, Rapidus will expand its CORE offerings beyond design to include EDA, IP and other categories. Rapidus is a Japanese state-backed semiconductor company founded in 2022 to mass-produce cutting-edge two-nanometer logic chips domestically by 2027. It was established through a partnership between the Japanese government and major private corporations, including Toyota, Sony, NTT, and SoftBank, to reduce Japan's reliance on foreign chipmakers like TSMC. title: MKH bakal dinyahsenarai selepas Batu Kawan kuasai 95.16% saham | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt – MKH Bhd bakal dinyahsenarai daripada Bursa Malaysia selepas Batu Kawan Bhd bersama anak syarikatnya, Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd serta pihak yang bertindak bersama mereka menguasai 95.16% saham syarikat pemaju hartanah itu. Jumlah pegangan tersebut bersamaan 548.85 juta saham MKH setakat penutupan dagangan pada 30 Sept 2026, menurut kenyataan yang dikeluarkan oleh Maybank Investment Bank Bhd bagi pihak Batu Kawan dan Whitmore. Dengan pegangan yang sudah melepasi 90%, Batu Kawan dan Whitmore kini boleh mengambil alih baki saham MKH yang masih dipegang pemegang saham yang tidak menerima tawaran pengambilalihan tersebut. Baki saham MKH akan diambil alih secara wajib Langkah itu akan dibuat di bawah Seksyen 222(1) Akta Pasaran Modal dan Perkhidmatan 2007 yang membolehkan baki saham diperoleh secara wajib. Tawaran pengambilalihan pada harga RM2 sesaham itu masih dibuka sehingga 8 Oktober 2026 selepas tarikh tutup asal pada 17 September lalu dilanjutkan. Selepas tempoh tawaran tamat, Bursa Malaysia Securities akan menggantung dagangan saham MKH selepas lima hari pasaran, sebelum Batu Kawan dan Whitmore meneruskan proses untuk menarik balik status penyenaraian MKH. Pengambilalihan MKH bernilai RM1.15 bilion Langkah Batu Kawan mengambil alih MKH bermula pada Mei lalu apabila Whitmore bersetuju membeli kepentingan 47.7% dalam MKH daripada anggota keluarga Chen pada harga RM2 sesaham, membabitkan nilai RM549.8 juta. Pembelian itu kemudiannya disusuli tawaran kepada pemegang saham MKH yang lain pada harga sama bagi membolehkan Batu Kawan meningkatkan pegangannya dalam syarikat tersebut. Secara keseluruhan, pengambilalihan MKH untuk menjadikannya syarikat persendirian bernilai sehingga RM1.15 bilion, termasuk kos pembelian kepentingan awal daripada keluarga Chen. Tawaran RM2 sesaham terima pandangan berbeza Bagaimanapun, tawaran tersebut sebelum ini mendapat pandangan berbeza daripada penasihat bebas MKH dan MKH Oil Palm (East Kalimantan) Bhd, iaitu cabang perladangan MKH yang disenaraikan secara berasingan. Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd, yang bertindak sebagai penasihat bebas MKH, menilai tawaran RM2 sesaham itu sebagai “tidak adil tetapi munasabah”, dengan mengambil kira harga tawaran yang lebih rendah daripada nilai aset wajar MKH. Bagi MKH Oil Palm pula, Mainstreet Advisers Sdn Bhd menggesa pemegang saham menolak tawaran 66.26 sen sesaham daripada Batu Kawan, yang disifatkannya sebagai “tidak adil dan tidak munasabah”. Menurut Mainstreet, harga tawaran itu mewakili diskaun 47% kepada nilai aset bersih (NAV) MKH Oil Palm. Pada masa sama, Batu Kawan bercadang mengekalkan MKH Oil Palm sebagai syarikat yang disenaraikan di Bursa Malaysia.- DagangNews.com

title: Axis REIT ‘well positioned’ against rate risks amid RM250 mil deal pipeline — analyst
body: Axis REIT ‘well positioned’ against rate risks amid RM250 mil deal pipeline — analyst KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Longer-term financing secured much earlier is now providing Axis REIT (KL:AXREIT) cushion against rising interest rates as the real estate investment trust pursues deals, an analyst said. A 25-basis-point increase in policy rate would potentially raise its cost of borrowings by just 0.1 percentage-point to 4.06%, Maybank Investment Bank said, noting that Axis REIT has locked in 10-year and seven-year financing facilities over the past 12 months when rates were more favourable. “With the completion of signed acquisitions, gearing is expected to rise to around 39%, still having ample headroom before any equity raising is required,” the research house said. Axis REIT owns and manages more than 70 office and industrial assets worth over RM5 billion in Klang Valley, Penang, Johor, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan and Kedah. The trust is in the midst of acquiring a distribution centre, a warehouse, and an industrial complex for RM193 million combined. The stated aim is to nearly double the asset under management to RM10 billion by 2030, driven by high-growth sectors and key industrial hubs throughout Peninsular Malaysia. In the near term, Axis REIT has a RM250 million acquisition pipeline currently under negotiation, of which one or two transactions could be announced before year-end, Maybank Investment said and maintained its “buy” call on the trust. “We believe its acquisition pipeline should provide further income visibility” with most ongoing transactions fully occupied and carrying weighted average lease expiry of five years or longer, the research house said. Axis REIT has rebounded from its September lows when the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years, sending global bond yields higher and triggering concerns of rising borrowing costs. Still, 10 out of 12 research houses tracked by Bloomberg recommend investors to “buy” Axis REIT and two are on “hold” calls. The average target price is RM2.22, a potential gain of up to 21% in the next 12 months from current price of RM1.84. The content is a snapshot from Publisher.
